headline: Saad Baig targets bigger scores after impressive ODI debut
description: LAHORE - Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig is determined to turn promising starts into bigger scores and establish himself as a dependable performer.
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Saad Baig is determined to turn promising starts into bigger scores and establish himself as a dependable performer. Speaking on the PCB Digital programme Straight Drive with Salman Butt, the 20-year-old reflected on his ODI debut series, scoring 185 runs in five matches, including a maiden half-century, and taking three catches.Baig scored 74 in Pakistan’s three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka in the tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium.“My plan was to carry the confidence I developed in domestic cricket into international cricket, back my skills and play my natural game,” he said. He stressed the importance of adapting to match situations. “Sometimes you have to control your instincts and build a partnership according to the situation. I tried to do that while communicating with my batting partner. I am thankful to have contributed to the team’s success.” Baig progressed through Pakistan’s U13, U16 and U19 pathways before captaining Pakistan at the 2024 Under-19 World Cup. He described reaching the senior team as rewarding.“I am grateful for this positive start, but this is only the beginning. My focus is to keep learning, identify areas for improvement and develop my game to perform consistently for Pakistan,” he added.

headline: Ahmad Baig wins Q-School leg in Spain, steps closer to DP World Tour milestone
description: LAHORE - Pakistan’s premier golf sensation, Ahmad Baig, has written a remarkable chapter in the country’s sporting history by delivering a
author: Azhar Khan
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan’s premier golf sensation, Ahmad Baig, has written a remarkable chapter in the country’s sporting history by delivering a sensational performance at the DP World Tour Qualifying School Second Stage, held at the Desert Springs Resort in Almería, Spain. Displaying extraordinary composure, precision, and elite technical skill, Baig captured the top spot on the leaderboard in dominant fashion. Over the course of the rigorous qualifying rounds, he carded exceptional scores of 67, 63, 65, and 66, finishing with a staggering tournament total of 27-under-par (261). His breathtaking form left the rest of the international field trailing in his wake, allowing him to seal a resounding victory with a commanding five-shot cushion over his nearest competitors.

England’s Jack Yule and Zimbabwe’s Kieran Vincent shared second place at 22-under-par (266), while players like Jack Hawksby and Albin Bergstrom rounded out the top tier. Baig’s stellar scorecard, highlighted by a phenomenal 6-under-par final round, underscored his mental toughness and ability to perform under high-pressure conditions on foreign soil. With this triumph, Baig has successfully advanced to the Final Stage of the Qualifying School, which is set to take place at INFINITUM in Tarragona, Spain. There, a formidable field of 156 players will battle across six grueling rounds for highly coveted playing rights on the elite DP World Tour for the upcoming 2027 season. Securing a card would make Baig the first golfer from Pakistan to achieve full membership on Europe’s premier professional circuit, a groundbreaking milestone for the nation’s golfing landscape. Hailing from humble origins and rising through relentless self-belief and raw talent, Baig’s journey to the international stage has largely been a proof of his own grit, perseverance, and dedication. As he prepares to test his mettle against some of the world’s finest golfing champions in the final qualifier, sports enthusiasts and sports bodies across Pakistan are rallying behind him.

headline: Amin Mukaty clocks sub-three-hour finish at New York City Marathon
description: LAHORE - Pakistani distance runner Amin Mukaty has achieved a remarkable milestone by becoming the fastest Pakistani finisher at the New York City Marathon
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistani distance runner Amin Mukaty has achieved a remarkable milestone by becoming the fastest Pakistani finisher at the New York City Marathon 2026, completing the gruelling 42.195-kilometre race in an impressive time of two hours, 53 minutes and 42 seconds (2:53:42).

Mukaty’s sub-three-hour performance at one of the world’s most prestigious marathon events marks a proud moment for Pakistan and highlights his dedication, discipline and growing presence on the international running circuit. The achievement is also a significant milestone in his athletic journey, which has been supported by ACTIVIT through a comprehensive partnership covering medical, nutritional and financial assistance. As an ACTIVIT athlete and ambassador, Mukaty has benefited from the organisation’s support in preparing for international competitions and pursuing ambitious sporting goals.

Reflecting on his performance, Mukaty thanked Almighty Allah for helping him accomplish the feat, describing the New York race as an extremely challenging experience. He said he was the only Pakistani runner to finish this year’s event in under three hours.“I am proud to have completed the 42.195-kilometre race in 2:53:42. It was one of the toughestraces of the world, but achieving a sub-three-hour finish is a special moment for me, Pakistan and ACTIVIT,” he said.

He revealed that he was pursuing the ambitious goal of completing all six of the major international marathons he had set out to run, with only one remaining.“I am especially grateful to Rd. Rizwan Aftab Ahmed and ACTIVIT for their 360-degree support and motivation. Their encouragement has helped me remain focused on my goal. I am hopeful that, with the prayers and support of my family, well-wishers and ACTIVIT, I will complete the remaining marathon. It would be a great honour for me and my country,” he added. ACTIVIT also celebrated Mukaty’s achievement, describing its association with the athlete as a commitment extending beyond sponsorship to supporting his preparation, performance and representation of Pakistan on the international stage.His impressive New York performance is another landmark in his marathon career, while his ambition to complete the remaining major race promises another challenge in his pursuit of international excellence.

headline: Top players advance at 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis
description: LAHORE - Top players moved into the next rounds as the 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis Championship 2026 continued at the Sports Board
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Top players moved into the next rounds as the 10th Sheheryar Malik Memorial Pakistan Open Tennis Championship 2026 continued at the Sports Board Punjab Tennis Academy, Nishtar Park, Lahore, with competitive action across men’s singles, women’s singles and boys’ under-12 categories. In the men’s singles first round, Muhammad Shoaib made an emphatic start, defeating Saif Ullah 6-0, 6-2. Jabir Ali overcame Kamran Khan 6-4, 6-2, while Ali Talha beat Hamza Naeem 6-1, 6-1. Abubakar Talha also secured a straight-sets victory, defeating M. Ahtesham 6-1, 6-1.Other winners included Yousaf Khalil, who beat Ahmad Babar 7-5, 6-4; M. Junaid, who edged Ahmad Raza 7-5, 7-6; and Imran Bhatti, who recorded a 6-0, 6-0 win over Hamza Khan.

Talha Khan, Asad Zaman, Asad Ullah and Barkat Ullah also advanced. headline: Solano urges collective effort as Pakistan target SAFF last four
description: LAHORE - Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano has set qualification for the semi-finals as his immediate target at the SAFF Championship 2026, expressing
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan head coach Nolberto Solano has set qualification for the semi-finals as his immediate target at the SAFF Championship 2026, expressing confidence in his squad while emphasising collective responsibility, tactical discipline and the development of homegrown football talent. Addressing a press conference at a local hotel in Islamabad on Monday evening, the former Peru international acknowledged the challenges awaiting Pakistan but insisted that his side were well prepared to compete and had the belief to achieve their objectives.

Solano said Pakistan had gained valuable experience from their recent international assignments in the Maldives and Indonesia, adding that the team were gradually developing into a stronger and more competitive unit. “Every competition is tough, but we are looking forward to this challenge. We are trying to build a very strong side, and I don’t think we are too far away. We won in the Maldives and also played in Indonesia, so we understand the level of competition and know what we have to do,” he said. The head coach stressed that his players must approach both encounters with the intensity of knockout fixtures, beginning with Thursday’s high-profile clash against India.“We go step by step. We have a big game against India on Thursday, followed by the Maldives. Our focus is on these two matches and qualifying for the semi-finals. We have to treat every game as a final. The first final is against India and the second is against the Maldives,” he said. Highlighting the significance of the Pakistan-India rivalry, Solano compared its passion and intensity to the fiercely contested football encounters between Peru and Chile.“Peru versus Chile is just like Pakistan versus India. It carries the same intensity. I understand what these matches mean to the fans, and we want to make our people happy. These games are special, and that is motivation in itself,” he added. Solano underlined that Pakistan’s success would depend on unity and collective commitment rather than individual brilliance, stressing that the entire team must contribute equally in both attacking and defensive phases.“We have to stay together. Football is not an individual game; it is a collective effort. Whether we attack or defend, we must do it together,” he maintained.

The coach also addressed the absence of Pakistan’s diaspora-based players during the opening phase of the competition, which falls outside the FIFA international match window. However, he refused to view their unavailability as a setback, expressing full confidence in the country’s domestic footballers.

“At the beginning of the competition, we cannot bring our diaspora players because it is not being held during the FIFA window. However, we are giving opportunities to local boys and looking at the talent available here. There are no excuses. We believe in our players,” Solano said.

He further stressed that the national team’s doors would remain open to anyone capable of meeting the required standards of talent, commitment and professionalism.“The door is open to every player who has talent and the right mentality. We are gradually building our talent pool,” he added.

Discussing Pakistan’s defensive approach, Solano said establishing a solid defensive foundation would remain a priority, while acknowledging that maintaining concentration throughout the match was essential at international level.

Reflecting on Pakistan’s 4-0 defeat against Thailand at the FIFA ASEAN Cup in Indonesia, he said the experience had reinforced the importance of discipline and focus for the entire 90 minutes.“Our first priority is to become a solid team and avoid conceding goals. We have some very good defenders, but the defeat against Thailand taught us an important lesson. At this level, even one moment of lost concentration can prove very costly,” he explained.

Beyond the immediate challenge of the SAFF Championship, Solano highlighted the need for stronger domestic football structures, regular competition and professional development opportunities to improve Pakistan’s overall standard.

Drawing comparisons with Peru’s football development, he said young players needed proper club structures and consistent opportunities to develop their abilities.“We have the talent, but these young players need support and a proper structure, particularly through clubs. The same thing happened in my country, Peru. That is how our young players continued to improve,” he said.

Welcoming plans to introduce a professional football league in Pakistan next year, Solano described the development as a significant step towards improving players’ fitness, match readiness and overall professional standards.

He pointed out that the absence of structured pre-season preparations had been a major challenge for Pakistan’s current generation of footballers.“This generation needs to be physically fit and capable of covering more ground. It is great news that Pakistan is expected to have a professional league from next year. Our current players have never had a proper pre-season, which is one of the most important parts of a footballer’s preparation. It prepares you for the entire season. Hopefully, we will have that soon, Inshallah,” he said.

Solano also indicated that Pakistan’s formation and tactical approach would depend on the availability of players and the strengths of their opponents, emphasising flexibility as an important element of the team’s preparations.Pakistan will launch their SAFF Championship 2026 campaign against India on Thursday before taking on the Maldives in their second group fixture. With a place in the semi-finals firmly in sight, Solano will be looking to translate his confidence in the local players into performances capable of delivering the desired results.

We have a big game against India on Thursday, followed by the Maldives. Our focus is on these two matches and qualifying for the semi-finals. We have to treat every game as a final. The first final is against India and the second is against the Maldives,” he said. Highlighting the significance of the Pakistan-India rivalry, Solano compared its passion and intensity to the fiercely contested football encounters between Peru and Chile.“Peru versus Chile is just like Pakistan versus India. It carries the same intensity. I understand what these matches mean to the fans, and we want to make our people happy. These games are special, and that is motivation in itself,” he added. Solano underlined that Pakistan’s success would depend on unity and collective commitment rather than individual brilliance, stressing that the entire team must contribute equally in both attacking and defensive phases.“We have to stay together. Football is not an individual game; it is a collective effort. Whether we attack or defend, we must do it together,” he maintained.

The coach also addressed the absence of Pakistan’s diaspora-based players during the opening phase of the competition, which falls outside the FIFA international match window. However, he refused to view their unavailability as a setback, expressing full confidence in the country’s domestic footballers.

“At the beginning of the competition, we cannot bring our diaspora players because it is not being held during the FIFA window. However, we are giving opportunities to local boys and looking at the talent available here. There are no excuses. We believe in our players,” Solano said.

He further stressed that the national team’s doors would remain open to anyone capable of meeting the required standards of talent, commitment and professionalism.“The door is open to every player who has talent and the right mentality. We are gradually building our talent pool,” he added.

Discussing Pakistan’s defensive approach, Solano said establishing a solid defensive foundation would remain a priority, while acknowledging that maintaining concentration throughout the match was essential at international level.

Reflecting on Pakistan’s 4-0 defeat against Thailand at the FIFA ASEAN Cup in Indonesia, he said the experience had reinforced the importance of discipline and focus for the entire 90 minutes.“Our first priority is to become a solid team and avoid conceding goals. We have some very good defenders, but the defeat against Thailand taught us an important lesson. At this level, even one moment of lost concentration can prove very costly,” he explained.

Beyond the immediate challenge of the SAFF Championship, Solano highlighted the need for stronger domestic football structures, regular competition and professional development opportunities to improve Pakistan’s overall standard.

Drawing comparisons with Peru’s football development, he said young players needed proper club structures and consistent opportunities to develop their abilities.“We have the talent, but these young players need support and a proper structure, particularly through clubs. The same thing happened in my country, Peru. That is how our young players continued to improve,” he said.

Welcoming plans to introduce a professional football league in Pakistan next year, Solano described the development as a significant step towards improving players’ fitness, match readiness and overall professional standards.

He pointed out that the absence of structured pre-season preparations had been a major challenge for Pakistan’s current generation of footballers.“This generation needs to be physically fit and capable of covering more ground. It is great news that Pakistan is expected to have a professional league from next year. Our current players have never had a proper pre-season, which is one of the most important parts of a footballer’s preparation. It prepares you for the entire season. Hopefully, we will have that soon, Inshallah,” he said.

Solano also indicated that Pakistan’s formation and tactical approach would depend on the availability of players and the strengths of their opponents, emphasising flexibility as an important element of the team’s preparations.Pakistan will launch their SAFF Championship 2026 campaign against India on Thursday before taking on the Maldives in their second group fixture. With a place in the semi-finals firmly in sight, Solano will be looking to translate his confidence in the local players into performances capable of delivering the desired results.

headline: Faheem Khan’s three kids win golds at US Junior Gold Squash C’ship
description: LAHORE - Pakistan-born squash players Fiza Khan, Youssef Khan and Ibrahim Khan made their mark at the 2026 University of Pennsylvania Junior Gold Squash
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - Pakistan-born squash players Fiza Khan, Youssef Khan and Ibrahim Khan made their mark at the 2026 University of Pennsylvania Junior Gold Squash Championship, winning three gold medals in their respective age categories in Philadelphia. Held from October 30 to November 1, the tournament saw Fiza claim the girls U-19 title, Youssef win the boys U-15 crown and Ibrahim emerge as boys U-13 champion. Competing under the Pakistani flag, the three siblings proudly represented their heritage, with Pakistan’s flag displayed alongside their names in the official draws and live scoring screens. Their father, Muhammad Faheem Khan, a former professional squash player and international coach who serves as Head Squash Pro and Director of Squash at Life Time King of Prussia, Pennsylvania, described the achievement as one of the proudest moments of his life. He credited their success to years of hard work, discipline and dedication, expressing immense pride in seeing all three children win titles while representing Pakistan.

headline: Karachi crowned champions of Berger Paints Girls Basketball Series
description: LAHORE - Karachi emerged champions in the inaugural Berger Paints Najam Shaikh Memorial Triangular Girls Basketball Series, held in Larkana, with the host team
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: LAHORE - Karachi emerged champions in the inaugural Berger Paints Najam Shaikh Memorial Triangular Girls Basketball Series, held in Larkana, with the host team finishing runners-up and Sukkur securing third place. Karachi defeated Sukkur 10-4 and Larkana beat Sukkur 10-0 in the opening matches. In the final, Karachi outclassed Larkana by 28 points to claim the title. Dua Batool of Bahria College was named girls of the series, while Larkana’s Ghulam Fiza received emerging player award. Iman and 12-year-old Sarah Ashraf were also recognised for their promising performances. Prof Aneela Abro was declared the best organiser. At the closing ceremony, Principal Govt Arts and Commerce College Prof Dr Rizwan Gul was the chief guest, while DSO Larkana Mahfooz Makani attended as guest of honour. SBBA patron Ghulam Muhammad Khan thanked the Sindh Sports Department, Larkana district administration, education authorities, Berger Paints and Lok Sahit Trust for their support.

headline: Arsalan’s 88 helps Khizra reach City Zone T20 semis
description: LAHORE - Khizra Cricket Club stormed into the semifinals of the Raza Hameed Memorial City Zone T20 Club Cricket Championship after defeating New Union Club by
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: LAHORE - Khizra Cricket Club stormed into the semifinals of the Raza Hameed Memorial City Zone T20 Club Cricket Championship after defeating New Union Club by 28 runs in an entertaining quarterfinal at Ittefaq LCCA Cricket Ground. Batting first, Khizra posted 183-6 in their allotted 20 overs, powered by 43-ball 88 from M Arsalan. Hussain Ali contributed an unbeaten 31 and Mohsin Ali scored 21. Abubakar claimed two wickets for New Union. In reply, New Union were bowled out for 155 in 18.3 overs despite M Azeem’s 36 and Muneeb Zafar’s 27. Muaz Awan and Ahmed Iqbal claimed three wickets each, while Mohsin Irshad and Iman Tahir got two each. Arsalan was named player of the match. Khizra Club chairman Abid Hussain also presented him with a cash award. Abid congratulated the players, captain and team management, praising their teamwork, determination and professional approach, and expressed confidence in the side’s ability to maintain their winning momentum in the semifinals.

headline: 464 killed in 44,797 road accidents across Punjab in Oct: Rescue 1122
description: LAHORE - As many as 464 people were killed and 23,543 others seriously injured in 44,797 road traffic accidents across Punjab during October 2026, Rescue 1122
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LAHORE - As many as 464 people were killed and 23,543 others seriously injured in 44,797 road traffic accidents across Punjab during October 2026, Rescue 1122 said on Monday. According to a spokesperson, the Punjab Emergency Service rescued 233,210 victims while responding to 231,056 emergencies across the province during the month, according to the monthly operational performance report. Punjab Emergency Service (PES) Secretary Dr. Rizwan Naseer expressed serious concern over the rising number of road accidents and fatalities while reviewing the department’s operational performance. The report showed that Lahore recorded the highest number of road accidents at 7,874, followed by Multan with 2,838, Faisalabad 2,615, Gujranwala 2,092 and Sheikhupura 1,714. The highest number of fatalities was reported in Lahore with 35 deaths, followed by Sheikhupura with 31, Faisalabad 30, and Multan and Gujranwala with 24 each. The secretary urged motorcyclists to drive on the left side of the road and maintain a speed below 50 kilometres per hour, warning that every one-kilometre-per-hour increase in speed raised the risk of a fatal accident by four to five per cent. The report also recorded 1,726 fire emergencies and 94 drowning incidents across the province during October. The review meeting was attended by Directors PES, heads of various wings and the provincial monitoring officer, while district emergency officers joined through video link.

headline: Rs1.32bn project approved for modernisation of Sher Bagh Bahawalpur
description: BAHAWALPUR - Commissioner Bahawalpur Division Irfan Ali Kathia visited Sher Bagh and reviewed ongoing development projects, available facilities,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
BAHAWALPUR - Commissioner Bahawalpur Division Irfan Ali Kathia visited Sher Bagh and reviewed ongoing development projects, available facilities, infrastructure improvements and proposed future initiatives. During the visit, the Curator of Sher Bagh briefed the Commissioner on the upgradation, renovation and various development initiatives aimed at transforming the facility into a modern recreational destination. The briefing revealed that a PC-I worth Rs1.320588 billion had been approved for the modernization of Sher Bagh, improved animal care and provision of quality recreational facilities for visitors. An amount of Rs100 million had been allocated for the project during the financial year 2026-27. Under the project, a modern main entrance gate, general recreational area and dedicated parking facilities for cars and motorcycles would be developed. A veterinary complex and hatchery would also be established to ensure improved animal healthcare, management and breeding facilities.

The project further included construction of a modern slaughterhouse, café area and indoor zoo, along with an effective drainage system and various infrastructure improvements to enhance the overall environment. The briefing further highlighted plans for constructing modern enclosures and moats for animals including giraffes, hippopotamuses, leopards, pumas and wolves. A bird aviary, a dedicated pond for crocodiles and a new curator’s office would also be established. Existing habitats of bears, lions, hyenas, tigers, monkeys and other animals would be upgraded in accordance with modern requirements to ensure better living conditions and improved animal welfare. The development plan also envisaged extensive upgradation of the existing Wildlife Museum, renovation of the auditorium and inspection hut, restoration of the duck pond and removal of obsolete structures. To enhance biodiversity at Sher Bagh, the project included increasing the variety of animal species, establishing suitable breeding pairs and acquiring new animals. Commissioner Irfan Ali Kathia said all available resources would be utilized to transform Sher Bagh into a modern, attractive and quality recreational facility, providing a better environment for citizens, particularly children and families.

He directed the concerned officials to ensure high construction standards without compromise, accelerate the pace of development work and complete all schemes within their stipulated timelines. The Commissioner also emphasized transparency, efficient utilization of available resources and continuous monitoring of construction activities to ensure quality and timely execution of the project. Director Development Malik Mahboob Elahi Khar, Curator Sher Bagh, Wildlife Department officials and other concerned officers accompanied the Commissioner during the visit.

headline: Illegal medical stores, quacks thrive unchecked in Muzaffargarh, Layyah
description: MUZAFFARGARH - Young man in Kot Addu reportedly suffers severe reaction to prescribed medication; swelling of hands and feet and darkening of skin raise
author: Khurram Malazai
article_text:
MUZAFFARGARH - Young man in Kot Addu reportedly suffers severe reaction to prescribed medication; swelling of hands and feet and darkening of skin raise serious questions over health authorities’ oversight

Quackery operating under the guise of unlicensed and unregistered medical stores has reportedly become a growing concern in Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu and Layyah, putting the health and lives of unsuspecting citizens at risk. In a recent incident in Kot Addu, a young man reportedly suffered a severe adverse reaction after taking medication prescribed by an alleged quack operating at a local medical store. His condition allegedly deteriorated to the extent that he became bedridden, with his hands and feet swelling and dark discolouration appearing on his body. The incident has raised serious concerns about the effectiveness of the Health Department’s monitoring and the enforcement of drug control regulations in the region. Questions are also being raised about the alleged presence of unqualified practitioners at medical stores operating without valid licences or registration. The reported silence of the District Health Officer and the concerned Drug Inspector has further fuelled public concern. Residents are questioning why effective action has not been taken against illegal medical outlets and alleged quacks despite the potential risks to public health. Who will be held accountable if such incidents continue? Will the relevant authorities act before another serious medical tragedy occurs, and will the alleged negligence of officials responsible for enforcement be investigated? Citizens have urged senior government officials, the Punjab Health Secretary and the Drug Control Authority to take immediate notice of the matter, order an impartial investigation into the Kot Addu incident and launch an indiscriminate crackdown on unlicensed medical stores and unqualified practitioners across Muzaffargarh, Kot Addu and Layyah. They have also demanded accountability of officials responsible for ensuring compliance with healthcare and drug safety regulations.

headline: PPRA orders probe into IBTS Lab equipment purchase
description: LAHORE - The Punjab Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) has raised serious concerns over the evaluation process adopted in the procurement of CLIA kits and
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - The Punjab Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) has raised serious concerns over the evaluation process adopted in the procurement of CLIA kits and fully automated analyzers for the Institute of Blood Transfusion Services (IBTS), Punjab. The authority in an order dated October 26, 2026 copy of which is available, referred the matter to the Specialized Healthcare and Medical Education Department for an independent inquiry into allegations of irregularities for purchase lab equipments including the purported supply and installation of refurbished machinery. The order passed on a representation filed by Roche Pakistan Limited, PPRA observed that the use of ambiguous and subjective technical terminology in bidding documents creates room for arbitrariness and may provide opportunities to manipulate competition. The authority emphasized that procurement specifications must be clear, precise and based on objectively verifiable criteria rather than subjective interpretations. The controversy arose from the technical evaluation of bids for the procurement of CLIA kits, along with fully automated, brand-new and latest-model analyzers on a reagent rental basis for ten blood transfusion units for the financial year 2026–27. Following the evaluation process, Roche Pakistan was declared technically non-responsive, leaving only one bidder, Abbott Laboratories Pakistan Limited, technically qualified for the procurement.

The development has raised questions regarding the narrowing of competition, particularly as Roche Pakistan had been supplying these testing solutions to the IBTS for the preceding four years, with its contract extended during the pendency of the procurement proceedings. The exclusion of an established supplier, coupled with the qualification of only one bidder, has brought the transparency and competitiveness of the evaluation process under scrutiny. Roche Pakistan had alleged that the analyzers supplied and installed by the successful bidder were refurbished rather than brand-new, contrary to the requirements of the bidding documents. The tender specifically required fully automated, brand-new and latest-model analyzers. PPRA observed that these allegations required factual verification, including examination of the machinery’s condition, age, import history, installation records and technical specifications. Consequently, the authority referred the matter to the Secretary, Specialized Healthcare and Medical Education Department, Punjab, with the advice to constitute an independent inquiry committee comprising representatives of the administrative department and proficient technical experts to investigate the allegations concerning the supply and installation of refurbished machinery. The order further underscores the importance of objective and transparent technical evaluations in public procurement, particularly where the procurement involves critical diagnostic equipment directly connected with public health and the safety of blood transfusion services. The matter has once again brought into focus the need for effective institutional oversight, fair competition and adherence to procurement principles. The restriction of competition to a single technically qualified bidder, despite the participation of an established supplier with a four-year supply history, alongside unresolved allegations regarding the condition and conformity of supplied machinery, raises serious reservations requiring transparent and impartial scrutiny. The inquiry directed by PPRA is expected to establish the factual position and ensure that public procurement is conducted in accordance with the principles of transparency and competition.

headline: Two-day international conference ICAZ-2026 begins at GCUF
description: FAISALABAD - The two day International Conference on Applied Zoology (ICAZ-2026) commenced at Government College University Faisalabad (GCUF) in collaboration
author: Staff Reporter
article_text: FAISALABAD - The two day International Conference on Applied Zoology (ICAZ-2026) commenced at Government College University Faisalabad (GCUF) in collaboration with the Applied Zoological Society of Pakistan. The conference brought together scientists, researchers, academicians and students from 19 international and 36 Pakistani universities. Professor Dr Iqrar Ahmad Khan Chairman of the Punjab Higher Education Commission (PHEC) attended the conference as the chief guest, while Professor Dr Rauf-i-Azam, Vice Chancellor of Government College University and Professor Dr. Muhammad Ali Vice Chancellor of the University of the Punjab served as Chief Patrons. Professor Dr Farhat Jabeen served as the Patron of the conference and welcomed the participants. Vice chancellors and distinguished experts from various universities also attended the event. Addressing the gathering Vice Chancellor Professor Dr Rauf-i-Azam described the conference as a significant initiative for promoting scientific research, higher education and international academic collaboration. He emphasised that such academic activities play a vital role in enhancing the research capabilities of faculty members and students while creating new opportunities for national and international research partnerships. Professor Dr Muhammad Ali highlighted the importance of the conference as an effective platform for researchers to exchange scientific knowledge, research findings and practical experiences. He also shed light on the history and contributions of the Applied Zoological Society of Pakistan. Professor Dr. Farhat Jabeen emphasized the importance of scientific research in conserving biodiversity, addressing environmental challenges, maintaining ecological balance and promoting sustainable development.

headline: NBP observes Pinktober 2026
description: KARACHI - National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) observed Pinktober 2026 through a series of breast cancer awareness initiatives aimed at promoting early detection,
author: PR
article_text:
KARACHI - National Bank of Pakistan (NBP) observed Pinktober 2026 through a series of breast cancer awareness initiatives aimed at promoting early detection, timely medical consultation, and employee well-being.

As part of the campaign, NBP’s head office organized a breast cancer awareness session on October 12, 2026, at the NBP Auditorium, in collaboration with Pink Ribbon Pakistan. The session highlighted the importance of recognizing potential warning signs, seeking timely medical advice, and encouraging open conversations about breast health.

Speaking on the occasion, Imran Sarwar, President & CEO, National Bank of Pakistan, emphasized the importance of prioritizing health and well-being alongside professional responsibilities. He highlighted the role of awareness, timely medical consultation, and a supportive workplace in enabling individuals to make informed decisions about their health. He reaffirmed the bank’s commitment to fostering a workplace culture that values employee well-being.

Mirza Muhammad Asim Baig, Group Chief, Human Resource Management Group (HRMG), underscored the importance of incorporating employee well-being into the Bank’s people-focused initiatives. He highlighted the value of promoting awareness, encouraging open dialogue, and providing access to reliable health information in building a healthier and more supportive workplace.

Saman Abbasi, Divisional Head - Capability, Culture & Corporate Impact, emphasized the role of awareness and education in encouraging employees to take proactive steps towards their health. She noted that initiatives such as Pinktober help address misconceptions, promote informed conversations, and reinforce the importance of early detection and timely medical guidance.

The campaign extended beyond head office, with NBP’s staff colleges and regional teams organizing awareness sessions and activities to engage employees across locations. These initiatives provided opportunities for employees to learn from healthcare professionals, address common misconceptions, and strengthen their understanding of breast cancer awareness and early detection.

headline: Awareness session for livestock farmers
description: FAISALABAD - The Livestock and Dairy Development Department Punjab organised an awareness session for livestock farmers and stakeholders in Faisalabad to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
FAISALABAD - The Livestock and Dairy Development Department Punjab organised an awareness session for livestock farmers and stakeholders in Faisalabad to provide guidance on modern livestock development initiatives. During the session Dr. Sohail Manzoor Director Breed Improvement Punjab, delivered a detailed briefing on the objectives and key features of the ADP scheme titled “CM Punjab Herd Transformation to Enhance Livestock Productivity.” Dr Riffat Senior Veterinary Officer, Directorate of Breed Improvement Punjab, conducted a technical session highlighting modern breeding technologies, genetic improvement and the importance of artificial insemination. On the occasion, Dr. Rubina Anjum Additional Director Livestock Faisalabad thanked the speakers and emphasized the department’s commitment to improving the delivery of modern breeding technologies, genetic improvement, animal tagging and traceability and strengthening the role of Artificial Insemination Technicians (AITs) to ensure that livestock farmers benefit from these facilities at their doorstep.

She termed the scheme an important milestone in the farmer friendly initiatives of Chief Minister of Punjab, Maryam Nawaz Sharif, aimed at enhancing livestock productivity and supporting the livestock farming community.

headline: Balochistan govt warns legal action against those spreading fake news
description: QUETTA - Aide to the Chief Minister of Balochistan on Media and Political Affairs, Shahid Rind, has said that fake news has emerged as a serious challenge and
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
QUETTA - Aide to the Chief Minister of Balochistan on Media and Political Affairs, Shahid Rind, has said that fake news has emerged as a serious challenge and the government has decided to initiate legal action against individuals found involved in spreading false information. Addressing a press conference at the Quetta Press Club on Monday, Shahid Rind said that anyone found disseminating fake news would face action in accordance with the law. He added that a formal complaint had already been submitted to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) regarding a fabricated report linked to the Chief Minister House and state institutions.

He said extensive discussion had taken place over the past two to three days regarding a particular news item, adding that the Government of Balochistan had repeatedly clarified its position during post-cabinet meeting briefings and stressed that fake news remains a major concern. Shahid Rind added that whenever the government has concerns regarding a news report, it shares the matter with the Quetta Press Club and the Balochistan Union of Journalists (BUJ). He added that action was also under way against Obaid Agha, Dr Sana and Maqbool Jaffar in connection with the fake news controversy involving the Chief Minister House and security institutions.

Responding to journalists’ questions, he acknowledged the growing importance of social media but stressed that character assassination under the guise of journalism could not be tolerated. Referring to a seminar organised by the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists (PFUJ), he said there must be an appropriate forum to address cases of defamation and character assassination, adding that the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) was enacted to deal with such matters. The assistant said the issues raised by the Balochistan Union of Journalists and the Quetta Press Club regarding private television channels and mainstream media had been taken up with the provincial government. While private TV channels do not fall directly under the provincial government’s jurisdiction, he said the government was playing its moral and facilitative role in addressing related concerns. Shahid Rind further remarked that media professionals should fulfil their professional responsibilities with due diligence and adherence to journalistic ethics. He emphasised that freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and in accordance with the law.

headline: SAU holds consultative session on Sindh Youth, Sports Policy 2026
description: HYDERABAD - Sindh Agriculture University (SAU), Tandojam held a consultative session on the proposed Sindh Youth and Sports Policy 2026, with a large number of
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: HYDERABAD - Sindh Agriculture University (SAU), Tandojam held a consultative session on the proposed Sindh Youth and Sports Policy 2026, with a large number of students actively participating in discussions on education, employment, entrepreneurship, sports and youth empowerment. The students shared their views and recommendations on issues affecting young people across the province. According to an SAU spokesperson, the consultation also focused on skills development, youth leadership, health and wellbeing, digital innovation, climate change and the empowerment of rural youth. Speaking on the occasion, Prof Dr Muhammad Ismail Kumbhar, Chairman of the Students-Teachers Engagement Programme (STEP) said young people were a driving force behind social transformation, economic progress, agricultural innovation and sustainable development. He stressed that their meaningful participation in policymaking was essential to develop inclusive and responsive policies. He said universities had a significant responsibility to prepare young people for emerging challenges through quality education, research, practical training and leadership development. He particularly highlighted the need to create opportunities for rural youth in agricultural entrepreneurship, food security, modern farming practices and sustainable livelihoods. Dr Kumbhar appreciated the enthusiastic participation of students, saying young people should not be regarded merely as beneficiaries of development programs but recognised as active partners in innovation, leadership and decision-making.

headline: One killed, two injured in Dadu road accident
description: DADU - One person was killed and two others sustained injuries in a road accident occurred on Dadu Bypass area. Initial reports said that a rashly driven
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: DADU - One person was killed and two others sustained injuries in a road accident occurred on Dadu Bypass area. Initial reports said that a rashly driven truck collided with a car passing through Dadu Bypass area of Sindh. As a result of collision, one person died on the spot while two others were injured. Following the incident, rescue team rushed to the site and shifted the body and injured to hospital. Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the exact cause of the accident.

headline: Sukkur mayor clarifies road development delays, says work on Qureshi Road, Gadani Phatak Project underway
description: SUKKUR - Mayor Sukkur and Spokesperson for Sindh government Barrister Arsalan Islam Shaikh, in a video message on Monday, clarified the misinformation
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: SUKKUR - Mayor Sukkur and Spokesperson for Sindh government Barrister Arsalan Islam Shaikh, in a video message on Monday, clarified the misinformation circulating on social media regarding the ongoing development work on various roads of Sukkur, shifting of electricity poles and roads linked with Qureshi Road and Gadani Phatak Overhead Bridge, stating that the development work is in progress and facts need to be seen from the right perspective. Barrister Arsalan Islam Shaikh said that in the context of the video surfacing regarding Qureshi Road and the debate on social media, he wants to clarify that the work order for this project was issued in June 2025, which can also be verified from the portal of the Sindh Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (SPPRA). Under the project, a total of 50 percent payment has so far been made to the contractor. The mayor said that there were previously 22 electricity poles on the road connected with the Gadani Phatak Overhead Bridge, of which 11 poles have been shifted. The work of widening the road and converting it into a dual carriageway has also been carried out. Now, only the asphalt (carpeting) work remains on the entire road, which is to be completed. Therefore, projecting this project as incomplete and giving the impression that no work has been done here is not correct. He further said that for the shifting of electricity poles and to eliminate potential risks of accidents, the Sukkur Municipal Corporation had taken up the matter with SEPCO in 2022. In this regard, a challan of about Rs33.9 million was issued, which was paid by the Sukkur Municipal Corporation. However, due to an increase in the volume of work and delays on part of SEPCO, it took time for the matter to proceed. The mayor informed that in SEPCO’s letter dated January 31, 2023, along with confirmation of the previous payment, an additional demand of Rs2.7 million was made. The Sukkur Municipal Corporation, instead of getting into any dispute, also paid this amount in June 2024. Later, due to no progress in work for about two years, a new challan of Rs2.4 million was issued based on price escalation, which was also paid within about one and a half months of its issuance in October. He said that these payments and related documents clearly show that the Sukkur Municipal Corporation did not evade its responsibilities but provided the required financial resources for shifting of electricity poles despite limited resources. Some delay was caused by SEPCO; however, SEPCO has also cooperated in various projects and where it has completed the work, its role is appreciated. He added that during development works on several important roads of Sukkur, with the cooperation of SEPCO, the roads were converted into dual carriageways after timely shifting and realignment of electricity poles, and later asphalt work was also completed.

headline: DC visits govt schools to review educational facilities
description: SUKKUR - Deputy Commissioner Shikarpur Dr Sharjeel Noor on Monday visited Government Qazi Habibullah School and Government Girls Primary School to review the
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: SUKKUR - Deputy Commissioner Shikarpur Dr Sharjeel Noor on Monday visited Government Qazi Habibullah School and Government Girls Primary School to review the educational situation and assess the facilities available at the institutions. During the visit, the deputy commissioner inspected classrooms and interacted with students to obtain information about their educational activities, studies and teaching process. He also reviewed teachers’ attendance, cleanliness, basic facilities and the overall educational environment at the schools. Dr Sharjeel Noor directed the school administrations concerned to ensure the provision of quality education to students, regular attendance of teachers and a better learning environment in the institutions. He further stated that the district administration would continue to play its role in improving the performance of educational institutions and ensuring the provision of educational facilities in government schools.

headline: 15 arrested, 435 mobile phones recovered in crackdown on illegal phone trade
description: KARACHI - Central District Police have arrested 15 suspects allegedly involved in the illegal purchase and sale of mobile phones and IMEI tampering, recovering
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KARACHI - Central District Police have arrested 15 suspects allegedly involved in the illegal purchase and sale of mobile phones and IMEI tampering, recovering 435 mobile phones worth millions of rupees, SSP Central Dr Imran Khan said on Monday. Addressing a press conference at his office, he said the raids were conducted in Khawaja Ajmer Nagri, New Karachi, Taimuria and Gulbahar areas. He said shopkeepers from mobile phone markets were also among the arrested suspects. The recovered items included 37 phones with tampered IMEI numbers, nine stolen Android phones and several expensive iPhones. Police also seized five computers and seven laptops allegedly used to alter the identity of mobile phones, he added.

The SSP said the suspects used to change the IMEI numbers of stolen and snatched mobile phones before selling them in the market. The recovered phones, worth millions of rupees, would be handed over to their original owners after verification, he said. Meanwhile, Sindh Home Minister Zia-ul-Hassan Lanjar appreciated DIG West, SSP Dr Imran Khan and his team for the successful operation. He said Central District Police had dismantled a criminal network through professional expertise and effective strategy, adding that the recovery of 435 stolen mobile phones reflected the police force’s dedication, hard work and effective policing.

headline: Karachi mayor says development projects underway across all seven districts without discrimination
description: KARACHI - Karachi Mayor Barrister Murtaza Wahab has said that development work has resumed in Karachi after a prolonged period, with development projects
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KARACHI - Karachi Mayor Barrister Murtaza Wahab has said that development work has resumed in Karachi after a prolonged period, with development projects underway across all seven districts of the city without discrimination. Sindh is the only province in Pakistan with an established local government system, while Karachi is a unique city where the mayor and town chairmen belonging to different political parties are working together to address public issues. He said that ongoing development activities demonstrate that the local government system is functioning effectively. Instead of making excuses about a lack of powers and resources, there is a need for commitment and practical action. We took the initiative and started working, and development activities have now begun in various towns across the city.

He expressed these views while addressing a press conference on ongoing development projects at the KMC Head Office on Monday. Pakistan Peoples Party Parliamentary Leader in the City Council Karamullah Waqasi, Deputy Parliamentary Leader Dil Muhammad, City Council Member Musarrat Niazi and others were also present on the occasion.

Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab said that Karachi is the industrial capital of Pakistan, and when the present administration assumed responsibility for the city, sewage treatment facilities were almost non-existent. The Pakistan Peoples Party had pledged in its manifesto to undertake sewage treatment projects for the people of Karachi, and practical progress had been made in this regard.

He said that with the support of the PPP leadership, Pakistan’s first industrial wastewater treatment project was completed in Karachi and inaugurated by Chairman Pakistan Peoples Party Bilawal Bhutto Zardari. The foundation stone for an additional wastewater treatment facility with a capacity of 65 million gallons per day was also laid. Efforts are underway to complete this project during the first quarter of next year. Upon its completion, a total of 100 million gallons of wastewater per day will be treated at the Haroonabad and Gutter Baghicha facilities. This is a significant achievement, and the credit goes to the people of Karachi and their elected representatives, he said.

The mayor said that providing healthcare and sports facilities was also among the administration’s top priorities. During the tenure of Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Karachi’s first sports complex was established on Kashmir Road. However, no major international-standard sports complex was constructed in the city for a long time thereafter. Under the present City Council and the leadership of the Pakistan Peoples Party, a state-of-the-art sports complex has been constructed in Baldia Town, district Keamari. The facility was inaugurated by PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, providing modern sports facilities to residents of an underdeveloped area.

Speaking about Spencer Eye Hospital, Mayor Wahab said that the decision to establish this historic institution was taken in 1938, and it became operational in 1940. The local leadership at the time established the hospital to provide treatment for eye diseases to citizens. In 1976, following an earthquake in Balochistan, the hospital’s staff and ambulances also participated in relief activities.

However, the institution was neglected in subsequent years, and by 2022–23, its condition had deteriorated to the extent that surgeries and other medical services were no longer being provided.

He said that the administration decided to restore the hospital’s functionality, and approval for a Public-Private Partnership project was obtained from the City Council, with the support of Pakistan Peoples Party members and its coalition partners. Today, approximately 350 patients benefit from outpatient department (OPD) services at Spencer Eye Hospital every day. These patients come from different parts of Karachi, including Lyari, Saddar, Baldia, Maripur, Malir, Korangi, and the East and Central districts. Patients from Balochistan and South Punjab also visit the hospital for treatment.

The mayor added that cataract surgeries and laser treatment facilities were being provided free of charge. At private hospitals, cataract surgery costs between Rs30,000 and Rs35,000, and can go up to Rs100,000. However, citizens are receiving this treatment entirely free of charge at Spencer Eye Hospital. On average, 60 to 70 patients benefit from cataract surgeries and related services every week. First Lady Aseefa Bhutto Zardari had also visited the hospital and met with patients, while PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and the Chief Minister of Sindh had attended the inauguration of the project. He said that the restoration of Spencer Eye Hospital demonstrated how historic institutions could be revitalised to provide quality healthcare services to the public.

Regarding sanitation and waste management, the mayor said that three modern Garbage Transfer Stations (GTS) were being established in the city. One is being constructed in Qayyumabad, near the Baloch Colony Expressway; the second in Sharafi Goth; and the third in Gutter Baghicha. Work on all three projects is in its final stages, and they are expected to become operational by the end of the current year. These facilities will enable waste to be collected mechanically and transported to landfill sites through an improved system.

Sindh is the only province in Pakistan with an established local government system, while Karachi is a unique city where the mayor and town chairmen belonging to different political parties are working together to address public issues.  He said that ongoing development activities demonstrate that the local government system is functioning effectively. Instead of making excuses about a lack of powers and resources, there is a need for commitment and practical action. We took the initiative and started working, and development activities have now begun in various towns across the city.

He expressed these views while addressing a press conference on ongoing development projects at the KMC Head Office on Monday.  Pakistan Peoples Party Parliamentary Leader in the City Council Karamullah Waqasi, Deputy Parliamentary Leader Dil Muhammad, City Council Member Musarrat Niazi and others were also present on the occasion.

Mayor Karachi Barrister Murtaza Wahab said that Karachi is the industrial capital of Pakistan, and when the present administration assumed responsibility for the city, sewage treatment facilities were almost non-existent. The Pakistan Peoples Party had pledged in its manifesto to undertake sewage treatment projects for the people of Karachi, and practical progress had been made in this regard.

He said that with the support of the PPP leadership, Pakistan’s first industrial wastewater treatment project was completed in Karachi and inaugurated by Chairman Pakistan Peoples Party Bilawal Bhutto Zardari. The foundation stone for an additional wastewater treatment facility with a capacity of 65 million gallons per day was also laid. Efforts are underway to complete this project during the first quarter of next year. Upon its completion, a total of 100 million gallons of wastewater per day will be treated at the Haroonabad and Gutter Baghicha facilities. This is a significant achievement, and the credit goes to the people of Karachi and their elected representatives, he said.

The mayor said that providing healthcare and sports facilities was also among the administration’s top priorities. During the tenure of Shaheed Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, Karachi’s first sports complex was established on Kashmir Road. The local leadership at the time established the hospital to provide treatment for eye diseases to citizens. In 1976, following an earthquake in Balochistan, the hospital’s staff and ambulances also participated in relief activities. 

However, the institution was neglected in subsequent years, and by 2022–23, its condition had deteriorated to the extent that surgeries and other medical services were no longer being provided.

These facilities will enable waste to be collected mechanically and transported to landfill sites through an improved system.

headline: Report of alleged inDrive data leak in Central Asia raises privacy questions for Pakistani users
description: Islamabad - Reports of a possible large-scale personal data breach in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have raised concerns over the security of customer information,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Islamabad - Reports of a possible large-scale personal data breach in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have raised concerns over the security of customer information, with databases of ride-hailing service inDrive allegedly exposed as well as other brands including cinema chain Kinopark and Lucem Medical Clinic report. The alleged customer data leak involving ride-hailing service inDrive in Central Asia has raised questions about the protection of personal information on a platform also used in Pakistan. The report concerns Kazakhstan as well as Uzbekistan and does not establish that Pakistani users’ data has been affected.

According to Kazakhstan-based news outlet Liter.kz, the Telegram channel Egov.Press claimed to have obtained evidence of the alleged data leaks involving the three organisations. Separately, a report from Uzbekistan (https://rus.azattyq-ruhy.kz/world/118398-v-uzbekistane-soobshchili-ob-utechke-dannykh-polzovatelei-indrive-i-drugikh-onlain-servisov), alleged that data linked to inDrive and several other platforms—including SafeRoad, Delever, Lada Auto, KiwiTaxi, Fargo, Maktab.uz, Andalus and Urbandiler.uz—was circulating online. The report said a purported SafeRoad database screenshot showed personal and vehicle-related information; these claims have not been independently verified. The potentially exposed information reportedly includes customers’ names, dates of birth, telephone numbers, email addresses and details of spending on services. The data may also contain information about cinema bookings and planned medical examinations, raising concerns about the potential exposure of sensitive personal information. Following the reports, Liter.kz contacted Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs, seeking confirmation of the alleged breach and a legal assessment of the matter. The claims have not been independently verified, and no official confirmation of the alleged breach was included in the report. For users in Pakistan, the relevant question is whether any potential exposure was limited to Kazakhstan and whether local accounts of Pakistani citizens could be affected. The report does not answer those questions.

headline: GIMS Gambat announces Laparoscopic Workshop for surgery PGRs
description: SUKKUR - The Department of Gallstone Surgery at Pir Abdul Qadir Shah Jeelani Institute of Medical Sciences (PAQSJIMS), Gambat has announced a hands-on
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
SUKKUR - The Department of Gallstone Surgery at Pir Abdul Qadir Shah Jeelani Institute of Medical Sciences (PAQSJIMS), Gambat has announced a hands-on Laparoscopic Workshop for postgraduate trainees. According to GIMS Spokesperson Jameel Hyder on Monday, the workshop is exclusively for General Surgery Postgraduate Residents (PGRs) who are currently enrolled in any university or college and are undergoing training in General Surgery. The training module includes simulator-based proficiency assessment followed by hands-on training with real patients for those who demonstrate proficiency on the simulator. headline: Sindh governor visits Quaid-e-Azam’s birthplace, reviews preservation of historical artefacts
description: KARACHI - Sindh Governor Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi on Monday visited Wazir Mansion in Kharadar, the birthplace of the Father of the Nation, Quaid-e-Azam
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KARACHI - Sindh Governor Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi on Monday visited Wazir Mansion in Kharadar, the birthplace of the Father of the Nation, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. Director General Antiquities, Government of Sindh, Abdul Sattar Sheikh, and Assistant Director Wazir Mansion, Munir Khayal, welcomed the governor upon his arrival. During the visit, the governor inspected various sections of Wazir Mansion and viewed the room used by Quaid-e-Azam, his library and other historical artefacts associated with his life.

He paid tribute to Quaid-e-Azam’s historic struggle, remarkable leadership and invaluable services for the creation of Pakistan. The governor said that the 150th birth anniversary of the Father of the Nation, Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah would be commemorated on December 25 this year. Various events would be organised throughout December to familiarise the younger generation with Quaid-e-Azam’s life, struggle and vision. He said that Pakistan emerged as a result of Quaid-e-Azam’s tireless efforts, exceptional leadership and the prolonged political struggle of the Muslims of the subcontinent. Our forefathers played a decisive role in the establishment of an independent homeland through the power of their vote. Syed Muhammad Nehal Hashmi stated that Pakistan, as an independent and sovereign state, was the outcome of the political struggle and democratic resolve of the Muslims of the subcontinent. Under Quaid-e-Azam’s inspiring leadership, Muslims secured a separate homeland where they could live with freedom and dignity. The governor further said that Quaid-e-Azam’s golden principles of Faith, Unity and Discipline continued to guide the nation towards progress, stability and national cohesion. He emphasised the need to incorporate these principles into individual and collective lives and contribute actively to the development of the country. The governor directed the concerned authorities to take necessary measures for the further preservation and protection of the historical artefacts at Wazir Mansion.

On the occasion, DG Antiquities Abdul Sattar Sheikh and Assistant Director Wazir Mansion Munir Khayal presented the governor with an Ajrak, a traditional symbol of Sindh’s cultural heritage.

On the conclusion of the visit, the governor also recorded his remarks in the visitors’ book at Wazir Mansion.

headline: ECP launches pilot project in Kamber Shahdadkot to bridge 49,000-voter gender gap
description: LARKANA - Director General of the Election Commission of Pakistan, Nighat Siddique, alongwith Deputy Commissioner Kamber Shahdadkot Kamran Hussain Mushtaq, on
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: LARKANA - Director General of the Election Commission of Pakistan, Nighat Siddique, alongwith Deputy Commissioner Kamber Shahdadkot Kamran Hussain Mushtaq, on Monday inaugurated a pilot project at the Darbar Hall of the Deputy Commissioner’s Office, Kamber. The project has been launched by the Election Commission of Pakistan to increase women’s registration and eliminate the gender gap between male and female voters. On this occasion, President Pakistan Peoples Party and Chairman District Council Kamber Shahdadkot Haji Qamaruddin Gopang, Inayatullah Jamali, District Election Commissioner Kamber Shahdadkot, Additional Deputy Commissioner-I Zohaib Zameer Odhano, alongwith all stakeholders and officers of the relevant government departments, attended the meeting. While chairing the meeting, Nighat Siddique stated that there is a gender gap of approximately 49,000 voters between men and women in district Kamber Shahdadkot, and this campaign has been launched to eliminate this disparity. She said that the purpose of her visit was to seek the full cooperation of civil society, media and other relevant institutions to make this campaign successful. She explained that the major reasons behind this gap include financial difficulties faced by women, lack of awareness, transportation problems and several other challenges, due to which women are unable to obtain their Computerised National Identity Cards (CNICs). She emphasized that a CNIC is not only required for casting a vote but is also essential for various other important matters of daily life. She informed the participants that the Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan has issued instructions to NADRA to provide free CNICs to women. Friday will be designated specifically for women, and their photographs will also be taken by female NADRA staff members. The DG further stated that previously, the gender gap in district Kamber Shahdadkot was more than 11 percent, which has now been reduced to 8.2 percent through the joint efforts of Election Commission officials, the district administration and other stakeholders. She said that the remaining gap of 49,000 voters must now be eliminated. She added that women’s registration in Sri Lanka is higher compared to men, whereas the rate of women’s registration in Kamber district remains lower. To address this issue, 839 CBCs will be deployed to conduct door-to-door registration of women. She stressed the need for cooperation from political parties, adding that an increase in the number of registered voters would also benefit political parties. She further informed the meeting that mobile registration teams would be sent to different villages, while registration desks would also be established at various locations to facilitate people and provide registration services within their respective areas. Nighat Siddique stated that contact numbers of 23,000 women out of the total gender gap of 49,000 are available, and NADRA is sending them text messages. Registration teams will also be dispatched to their homes to facilitate their registration process. Highlighting the educational and communication situation in the district, she said that the literacy rate in Kamber Shahdadkot is 48 percent, while approximately one million people use mobile phones and 200,000 people use Facebook. She described this as a positive opportunity for raising awareness about the campaign. She expressed hope that when she visits the district again, the gender gap will have been eliminated through the collective efforts and full cooperation of the district administration, civil society, media and all relevant institutions. She further announced that the campaign for women’s registration and elimination of the gender gap will continue from November 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027.

On this occasion, President Pakistan Peoples Party and Chairman District Council Kamber Shahdadkot Haji Qamaruddin Gopang, Inayatullah Jamali, District Election Commissioner Kamber Shahdadkot, Additional Deputy Commissioner-I Zohaib Zameer Odhano, alongwith all stakeholders and officers of the relevant government departments, attended the meeting. While chairing the meeting, Nighat Siddique stated that there is a gender gap of approximately 49,000 voters between men and women in district Kamber Shahdadkot, and this campaign has been launched to eliminate this disparity. She said that the purpose of her visit was to seek the full cooperation of civil society, media and other relevant institutions to make this campaign successful. She explained that the major reasons behind this gap include financial difficulties faced by women, lack of awareness, transportation problems and several other challenges, due to which women are unable to obtain their Computerised National Identity Cards (CNICs). She emphasized that a CNIC is not only required for casting a vote but is also essential for various other important matters of daily life. She informed the participants that the Chief Election Commissioner of Pakistan has issued instructions to NADRA to provide free CNICs to women. Friday will be designated specifically for women, and their photographs will also be taken by female NADRA staff members. The DG further stated that previously, the gender gap in district Kamber Shahdadkot was more than 11 percent, which has now been reduced to 8.2 percent through the joint efforts of Election Commission officials, the district administration and other stakeholders. She said that the remaining gap of 49,000 voters must now be eliminated.
She added that women’s registration in Sri Lanka is higher compared to men, whereas the rate of women’s registration in Kamber district remains lower. To address this issue, 839 CBCs will be deployed to conduct door-to-door registration of women. She stressed the need for cooperation from political parties, adding that an increase in the number of registered voters would also benefit political parties.
She further informed the meeting that mobile registration teams would be sent to different villages, while registration desks would also be established at various locations to facilitate people and provide registration services within their respective areas.
Nighat Siddique stated that contact numbers of 23,000 women out of the total gender gap of 49,000 are available, and NADRA is sending them text messages. Registration teams will also be dispatched to their homes to facilitate their registration process.
Highlighting the educational and communication situation in the district, she said that the literacy rate in Kamber Shahdadkot is 48 percent, while approximately one million people use mobile phones and 200,000 people use Facebook. She described this as a positive opportunity for raising awareness about the campaign.
She expressed hope that when she visits the district again, the gender gap will have been eliminated through the collective efforts and full cooperation of the district administration, civil society, media and all relevant institutions.
She further announced that the campaign for women’s registration and elimination of the gender gap will continue from November 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027.

headline: Sindh CM, WB review $3.849b development portfolio, discuss steps to accelerate Sindh projects
description: KARACHI - Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah and World Bank Country Director Ms Bolormaa Amgaabazar held a high-level portfolio review meeting at CM
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
KARACHI - Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah and World Bank Country Director Ms Bolormaa Amgaabazar held a high-level portfolio review meeting at CM House on Monday, taking stock of implementation status, financial progress, procurement activities, and outstanding challenges for World Bank-financed development projects across the province. The meeting reviewed 12 active operations, comprising 11 Investment Project Financing projects and one Programme-for-Results operation, with a combined commitment of $3.849 billion. Of this amount, $2.334 billion had been disbursed, while $1.571 billion remained undisbursed.

The participants also examined the financial and procurement performance of the projects, including the 2026-27 disbursement target of $381.2 million, with a stretch target of $434.2 million. Actual disbursements stood at $43.2 million. CM Murad Shah reaffirmed his government’s commitment to working closely with the World Bank to accelerate implementation, resolve administrative and financial bottlenecks and ensure that development investments translate into improved public services. He stressed that concerned departments and project teams must take ownership of pending actions, strengthen coordination, and meet agreed timelines. The Second Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP-2), of $240 million, was reviewed with particular attention to the K-IV associated facilities. The review noted that environmental and social instruments for the associated facilities had been prepared and submitted to the World Bank for clearance, while compliance monitoring was continuing. The revalidation survey for the K-IV augmentation resettlement action plan is scheduled to proceed shortly. The contract is expected to be signed on December 5, with the census and survey planned from December 21, 2026, to February 20, 2027. The meeting also reviewed the financial and operational reforms of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation. Several regulatory measures have been approved, while others, including service and wastewater recycling and reuse regulations, remain pending. The earlier Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP), which has closed, was also reviewed in terms of its outstanding completion activities. Rectification of the Dhabeji Rising Main has been completed, and chlorination stations have been relocated, commissioned and handed over to KW&SC. The second phase of water-quality testing is underway, while Soba Nagar and Essa Nagri water and sanitation works are expected to be completed by November 15 and December 31, respectively. Customer service centres are ready for inauguration by the end of November.

KARACHI MOBILITY AND SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT

The Karachi Mobility Project, which includes the Yellow Bus Rapid Transit corridor and associated road infrastructure, was reviewed with particular attention to the Jam Sadiq Bridge and bus depots. The newly constructed Taj Haider Bridge was opened to traffic in October 2025, while dismantling of the old bridge was in progress. The overall physical progress of the bridge project stood at 73.9 per cent against a planned 92.7 per cent, with completion scheduled for March 29, 2027. Work on the two Yellow Corridor bus depots is progressing at different stages. Depot-1 had achieved 17.57 percent progress against a planned 93.6 percent, while Depot-2 had achieved 46.66 percent against a planned 100 percent. Procurement for the BRT corridor packages is also moving forward: negotiations for Package 3B had commenced, while the combined evaluation of financial bids for Package 3A was underway. Technical bids for the two-lot Phase-II package were opened and are under evaluation.

The Solid Waste Emergency and Efficiency Project (SWEEP) was reviewed following the launch of operations at Cell-1 of the Jam Chakro landfill on October 19. The remaining landfill cells are at an advanced stage, and completion of the full landfill site is expected by November 30. Three garbage transfer stations at Sharafi Goth, Imtiaz and Gutter Baghicha are progressing towards completion by the same date. The landfill operations plan has been approved, while the garbage transfer station operations plan and a proposal for user-fee collection remain pending.

The Sindh Integrated Health and Population Project (SIHPP) of $196.7 million was reviewed in detail. The project has nine civil works contracts, all of which have been signed, with construction activities underway. The reconstruction and rehabilitation of health facilities across the province also came under discussion. The reported delays in the reconstruction of 12 Tehsil Headquarters hospitals are due to late handover of sites, tree-cutting and clearance issues, shifting of electricity poles and location-related complications at THQ Diplo. Overall completion of the 12 facilities is anticipated by September 2027. The procurement of 104 ambulances is also progressing. The contract is expected to be signed by January 1, 2027. The meeting also reviewed nutrition interventions, including the MoU signed between the Sindh government and UNICEF for the procurement of supplies.
