The meeting reviewed 12 active operations, comprising 11 Investment Project Financing projects and one Programme-for-Results operation, with a combined commitment of $3.849 billion. Of this amount, $2.334 billion had been disbursed, while $1.571 billion remained undisbursed.

The participants also examined the financial and procurement performance of the projects, including the 2026-27 disbursement target of $381.2 million, with a stretch target of $434.2 million. Actual disbursements stood at $43.2 million. CM Murad Shah reaffirmed his government’s commitment to working closely with the World Bank to accelerate implementation, resolve administrative and financial bottlenecks and ensure that development investments translate into improved public services. He stressed that concerned departments and project teams must take ownership of pending actions, strengthen coordination, and meet agreed timelines. The Second Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP-2), of $240 million, was reviewed with particular attention to the K-IV associated facilities. The review noted that environmental and social instruments for the associated facilities had been prepared and submitted to the World Bank for clearance, while compliance monitoring was continuing. The revalidation survey for the K-IV augmentation resettlement action plan is scheduled to proceed shortly. The contract is expected to be signed on December 5, with the census and survey planned from December 21, 2026, to February 20, 2027. The meeting also reviewed the financial and operational reforms of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation. Several regulatory measures have been approved, while others, including service and wastewater recycling and reuse regulations, remain pending. The earlier Karachi Water and Sewerage Services Improvement Project (KWSSIP), which has closed, was also reviewed in terms of its outstanding completion activities. Rectification of the Dhabeji Rising Main has been completed, and chlorination stations have been relocated, commissioned and handed over to KW&SC. The second phase of water-quality testing is underway, while Soba Nagar and Essa Nagri water and sanitation works are expected to be completed by November 15 and December 31, respectively. Customer service centres are ready for inauguration by the end of November.
KARACHI MOBILITY AND SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT

The Karachi Mobility Project, which includes the Yellow Bus Rapid Transit corridor and associated road infrastructure, was reviewed with particular attention to the Jam Sadiq Bridge and bus depots. The newly constructed Taj Haider Bridge was opened to traffic in October 2025, while dismantling of the old bridge was in progress. The overall physical progress of the bridge project stood at 73.9 per cent against a planned 92.7 per cent, with completion scheduled for March 29, 2027. Work on the two Yellow Corridor bus depots is progressing at different stages. Depot-1 had achieved 17.57 percent progress against a planned 93.6 percent, while Depot-2 had achieved 46.66 percent against a planned 100 percent. Procurement for the BRT corridor packages is also moving forward: negotiations for Package 3B had commenced, while the combined evaluation of financial bids for Package 3A was underway. Technical bids for the two-lot Phase-II package were opened and are under evaluation.

The Solid Waste Emergency and Efficiency Project (SWEEP) was reviewed following the launch of operations at Cell-1 of the Jam Chakro landfill on October 19. The remaining landfill cells are at an advanced stage, and completion of the full landfill site is expected by November 30. Three garbage transfer stations at Sharafi Goth, Imtiaz and Gutter Baghicha are progressing towards completion by the same date. The landfill operations plan has been approved, while the garbage transfer station operations plan and a proposal for user-fee collection remain pending.

The Sindh Integrated Health and Population Project (SIHPP) of $196.7 million was reviewed in detail. The project has nine civil works contracts, all of which have been signed, with construction activities underway. The reconstruction and rehabilitation of health facilities across the province also came under discussion. The reported delays in the reconstruction of 12 Tehsil Headquarters hospitals are due to late handover of sites, tree-cutting and clearance issues, shifting of electricity poles and location-related complications at THQ Diplo. Overall completion of the 12 facilities is anticipated by September 2027. The procurement of 104 ambulances is also progressing. The contract is expected to be signed by January 1, 2027. The meeting also reviewed nutrition interventions, including the MoU signed between the Sindh government and UNICEF for the procurement of supplies.

headline: Dawlance, Arcelik mark decade of partnership built on Pakistani talent and Turkish expertise
description: KARACHI - Dawlance, Pakistan’s leading home appliances manufacturer, is marking ten years as part of Arcelik, the Turkish home appliances group that
author: PR
article_text:
KARACHI - Dawlance, Pakistan’s leading home appliances manufacturer, is marking ten years as part of Arcelik, the Turkish home appliances group that acquired the company in 2016. Over the decade, the partnership has centred on transferring technology and skills from Turkiye to Pakistan and on developing local engineering talent.

Since the acquisition, Arçelik has invested more than Rs 14 billion in Pakistan, bringing the latest production machinery to Dawlance’s three plants and adding new lines for air conditioners, water dispensers, automatic washing machines and LED TVs, with products designed locally for Pakistani consumers. Dawlance today serves customers through around 2,000 dealers and over 400 customer-care touchpoints.

The partnership’s most lasting impact has been on people and skills. Dawlance engineers work closely with the group’s R&D teams in Turkiye, and the company now exports its design expertise as well as its products. Under a USD 2.6 million Design Export Project, Dawlance designed four refrigerator models for Singer Bangladesh, a fellow Arcelik subsidiary. Arçelik has also set up a Global Research & Development Center at the NUST in Islamabad, where Pakistani engineers develop software for home appliances across the group.

The same approach is deepening local manufacturing. In January 2026, Dawlance opened a condenser manufacturing facility where Pakistani engineers, working with engineering teams from Turkiye, designed and validated a component that was previously fully imported; around 75% of its value is now produced locally. One of Dawlance’s Karachi factories also now meets 20% of its power needs through solar energy.

headline: PPP to continue struggle for press freedom, protection of journalists: Bilawal
description: KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, in his message on the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: KARACHI - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, in his message on the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, has said that protecting journalists from serious crimes including threats, violence, harassment and murder was a shared responsibility of the state and society. He stressed that remaining silent on crimes against journalists or allowing perpetrators to escape punishment amounts to silencing the truth, denying justice and suppressing the public’s right to information. The PPP chairman said that journalists play a fundamental role in bringing facts to the public, holding the corridors of power to account, and raising awareness and consciousness in society. The escape of those involved in crimes against journalists from the grip of the law poses a grave threat to press freedom, democracy and the rule of law. Bilawal Bhutto Zardari said that the unanimous Constitution of 1973 guaranteed every citizen the fundamental right to freedom of expression and protecting this right was the constitutional and moral responsibility of a democratic state. He said that Shaheed Mohtarma Benazir Bhutto, during her first tenure in government, had abolished the black laws of the dictator Zia-ul-Haq’s era that were used to suppress press freedom and silence the voice of the press. This historic step, he said, expressed the resolve that democracy cannot do without space for dissent and a free press. The PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari reaffirmed that the PPP will continue its struggle for press freedom, freedom of expression and the protection of journalists, because without a free press, neither can democracy grow stronger nor can the people be kept informed and empowered.

headline: Sarsabz farmers claim all three provincial titles in Punjab’s Wheat Yield Competition 2025-26
description: LAHORE - Fatima Fertilizer celebrated farmers’ outstanding achievements at the Sarsabz Ki Jeet Wheat Yield Competition Prize Distribution Ceremony.
author: PR
article_text:
LAHORE - Fatima Fertilizer celebrated farmers’ outstanding achievements at the Sarsabz Ki Jeet Wheat Yield Competition Prize Distribution Ceremony. Farmers using Sarsabz Nitrophos and Calcium Ammonium Nitrate (CAN) secured the top three positions at the provincial level and 119 out of 120 district-level positions in the Punjab Wheat Yield Competition 2025–26, announced by the government of Punjab. Federal Minister for National Food Security & Research Rana Tanveer Hussain addressed the ceremony virtually. The event was also attended by Additional Chief Secretary (ACS), Punjab, Iftikhar Ali Sahoo, Secretary Agriculture Punjab, Shakeel Ahmad Mian and President Pakistan Kissan Ittehad Khalid Khokhar among other dignitaries.

Sarsabz farmers secured first position in 39 out of 40 districts and claimed all three provincial positions. Sajjad Hussain from Muzaffargarh secured first provincial position with a yield of 69 maunds and 39.4 kilograms per acre, followed by Shafiq Ahmed from Attock with 69 maunds and 39.1 kilograms per acre. Muhammad Asghar from Rahim Yar Khan secured third position with 69 maunds and 24.1 kilograms per acre. As part of the prize distribution, three tractors were awarded to the provincial winners. At the district level, Honda CD 70 motorcycles and LED TVs were presented to all district level positions.

headline: PTCL appoints Amad Khan as Chief Marketing Officer
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has announced the appointment of Amad Khan as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), following approval
author: PR
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) has announced the appointment of Amad Khan as Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), following approval by the company’s board of directors. Amad brings over two decades of experience across telecommunications, technology and digital transformation, with a career spanning Pakistan, Australia and the Middle East. His experience encompasses commercial strategy, product management, revenue growth, customer experience and large-scale technology transformation.

Since joining PTCL, Amad has held senior commercial leadership responsibilities across the company’s wireline portfolio, including Fiber, Voice, TV, OTT and IoT. He has played a pivotal role in advancing PTCL’s Fiber strategy, contributing to its position as Pakistan’s leading Fiber operator, while driving revenue growth, customer experience improvements and digital transformation initiatives. Prior to PTCL, Amad held senior roles at Optus Australia, where he contributed to Fiber and 5G Fixed Wireless Access strategy and led product and technology transformation initiatives. headline: Easypaisa Digital Bank BoD approves financial statements
description: ISLAMABAD - The board of directors of Easypaisa Digital Bank has approved the financial statements for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026. The bank
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The board of directors of Easypaisa Digital Bank has approved the financial statements for the nine-month period ended September 30, 2026. The bank announced its financial performance, reporting a profit before tax (PBT) of Rs 13.30 billion and profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 7.41 billion, representing a 2.35x increase in PBT over the corresponding period last year. Earnings per share (EPS) stood at Rs 12.31. The growth was broad-based across the bank’s core business streams, supported by an expanding customer base, rising transaction volumes, and continued investments in customer acquisition, talent, technology, and digital innovation.

Total revenue increased by 38.53% to Rs 46.67 billion year-on-year, reflecting strong momentum across lending, treasury and fee-based streams. Net markup income grew by 37.0%, supported by the expansion of the lending portfolio and treasury investments, underpinned by strong growth in customer deposits. Fee-based income increased by 40.63%, supported by higher revenues from payment services, including online payments, disbursements, collections and insurance products. Non-markup expenses increased to Rs 32.80 billion, in line with revenue growth, reflecting investment in customer acquisition, engagement and merchant penetration, as well as risk-sharing costs from higher digital lending volumes. The cost-to-income ratio was 70.27%.

Customer deposits grew by 59.06% year-on-year to Rs 174.39 billion, while maintaining a strong deposit mix with a CASA ratio of 96.99% and a current account ratio of 79%. Net advances reached Rs 31.65 billion, resulting in an advances-to-deposit ratio of 18.15%. Asset quality remained healthy, with non-performing loans at 2.91% of gross advances and a coverage ratio of 165.07%.

The bank remained adequately capitalised, with a capital adequacy ratio of 27.54% as of September 30, 2026, well above the regulatory requirement. Earlier this year, in July, the Pakistan Credit Rating Agency (PACRA) upgraded Easypaisa’s long-term entity rating to “AA-” and maintained its short-term rating at “A1”, recognising the bank’s strong financial performance, robust risk management, sound asset quality and improved capital position.

Commenting on the strong quarterly performance, Jahanzeb Khan, President & CEO, Easypaisa Digital Bank, said, “These results demonstrate that our growth as a digital bank is translating into strong and sustainable financial performance. With an expanding customer base, growing deposits and increasing adoption of digital financial services, we are building a broader digital banking ecosystem that goes beyond payments. Our focus now is to deepen customer relationships through lending, savings, remittances and Islamic banking, while continuing to advance financial inclusion and Pakistan’s digital economy.”

Easypaisa will continue to expand its digital ecosystem and lending portfolio and deepen customer engagement across foreign exchange, Islamic banking, credit cards, and remittance. The bank remains committed to advancing financial inclusion and Pakistan’s digital and cashless economy agenda.

headline: Pakistan could serve as key trade, transit corridor for Central Asian countries: Sheikh
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh has highlighted Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, seaport infrastructure
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh has highlighted Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, seaport infrastructure and investment potential as key opportunities for strengthening economic cooperation and regional connectivity with Central Asian countries.

Addressing the opening session of the Second TIANSHAN Forum for Central Asia Economic and Quality Investment in Almaty, Kazakhstan, the federal minister said that Pakistan could serve as an important trade and transit corridor for landlocked Central Asian countries, providing them with access to international maritime trade routes and global markets.

The minister highlighted Pakistan’s three major seaports — Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar Port — as strategic gateways that could facilitate regional trade, strengthen transportation links and provide alternative routes for the movement of goods. He particularly underscored Karachi’s importance as Pakistan’s major industrial and commercial hub, noting that its established industrial base, business infrastructure, financial institutions and port facilities offered significant opportunities for trade, industrial partnerships and foreign investment. He also highlighted Gwadar’s potential to further strengthen regional connectivity and economic cooperation.

Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh stated that Pakistan, with nearly 60 percent of its population comprising young people, enjoyed a significant demographic advantage in the form of a dynamic workforce and considerable potential for economic growth. He said that the government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, was focusing on strengthening regional connectivity, addressing energy requirements and creating an enabling environment to attract domestic and international investment.

The federal minister invited regional and international investors to explore opportunities in key sectors, including energy, infrastructure, logistics, transportation, manufacturing and trade. He emphasized that improved connectivity and reliable energy supplies were essential for unlocking the region’s economic potential.

Highlighting the importance of regional cooperation, the minister acknowledged the contribution of the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) Program in promoting transport connectivity, facilitating trade and supporting economic integration among participating countries.

He observed that CAREC provided a valuable platform for strengthening economic partnerships between Pakistan and Central Asian states.

The minister emphasized that Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, youthful population, industrial capacity and seaport infrastructure positioned the country to play an important role in connecting Central Asian economies with international markets.

Concluding his remarks, Qaiser Ahmad Sheikh stated that regional connectivity was not merely about linking roads, ports and markets, but also about connecting economies, creating investment opportunities, generating employment and building shared prosperity across the region.

headline: Ukraine defies Trump to resume attacks on Russian oil refineries
description: Kyiv - Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the US midterm elections, as a ceasefire in
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: Kyiv - Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries in defiance of pressure from Donald Trump ahead of the US midterm elections, as a ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky ended on Sunday night. Russian state media said on Sunday Ukrainian long-range drones had set fire to the Kstovo refinery in Nizhny Novgorod oblast overnight, soon after a major strike against another big refinery in Samara oblast, owned by the Russian state energy giant Rosneft. The Wall Street Journal had reported that Ukraine had given in to pressure from the White House to stop bombing Russian energy infrastructure. Ukrainian officials, however, told the Kyiv Independent newspaper that they never agreed to a demand from Jared Kushner, the US president’s son-in-law, to pause refinery strikes for 30 days.

headline: Hackers send fake nuclear threat alert to Ukraine emergency app
description: Kyiv - Unknown hackers have targeted Ukraine’s nationwide emergency alert mobile app, sending residents in Kyiv a warning that they were at risk of an
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: Kyiv - Unknown hackers have targeted Ukraine’s nationwide emergency alert mobile app, sending residents in Kyiv a warning that they were at risk of an imminent nuclear strike. The app reported a high possibility of nuclear radiation late on Sunday. It also wrongly warned of a chemical threat to the Ukrainian capital and street-to-street fighting. The messages were written in English with spelling mistakes, as well as in Ukrainian. Many residents ignored the alerts, which began shortly before 11pm local time, assuming that the app had been compromised. Others were scared. “I was briefly terrified,” one woman, Nina, said. “I lay on my bed and wondered what was coming.” A message written in Russian also claimed Ukraine was about to be hit by Oreshnik missiles, which can carry nuclear warheads. The Kremlin has used the ballistic weapon three times before, hitting the Kyiv region and the cities of Dnipro and Lviv. In a post on Sunday, the Ukrainian emergency app said “unauthorised parties” had interfered with its operation. The channel had been temporarily suspended, it said, warning users not to click on links in “suspicious notifications”. It was unclear on Monday who might have carried out the cyber-raid, or why. Russian officials claimed hackers had also sent fake emergency alerts there after gaining access to the app of the ministry for emergencies, based in Moscow.

headline: Israel maintains highest state of alert on eve of US midterm elections
description: Tel Aviv - Israel remained on the highest state of military alert on Monday, a day before the United States midterm elections, amid concerns over a
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Tel Aviv - Israel remained on the highest state of military alert on Monday, a day before the United States midterm elections, amid concerns over a possible resumption of war with Iran, according to Israeli media.

Americans head to the polls Tuesday for midterm elections halfway through Republican President Donald Trump’s second term, with all 435 seats in the House of Representatives, 35 Senate seats and governorships in 36 states up for grabs, alongside thousands of local positions and ballot measures. Trump has repeatedly pledged not to launch new strikes against Iran before the midterm elections, while suggesting that military operations could resume afterward, amid a continued US military buildup in the region and stalled diplomatic efforts. According to Israeli media, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government has been pushing for renewed strikes against Iran, ostensibly aimed at overthrowing its government, although Israeli officials acknowledge that the final decision rests with the White House.

Israeli news website Walla reported Monday that the military remained on high alert amid US and Israeli concerns that Iran could launch a surprise attack, either directly or through allied groups, against American interests in the region or Israel. The report said intelligence agencies fear Tehran could stage a large-scale military provocation that might influence the US midterm elections.

Walla said the Israeli military had intensified defensive and offensive preparations in recent weeks in coordination with US Central Command (CENTCOM) and the Pentagon.

Citing unnamed Israeli military officials, the website said security coordination between Israel and the US had reached its highest levels and that Israel would receive advance warning if Washington decided to attack Iran. However, Israeli military assessments suggest that the likelihood of a US preemptive strike before the midterm elections remains low, as Trump prefers to exhaust diplomatic negotiations and pressure before resorting to military action, according to the report.

Walla also said that more than 3,000 US troops were stationed in Israel, noting that no unusual increase in American military aircraft arrivals had been recorded over the past week, unlike the periods preceding previous escalations.

The report added that Israeli officials believe Tehran is seeking to buy time in negotiations with Washington, while disagreements persist over Iran’s nuclear program and ballistic missiles.

Tensions between Washington and Tehran have persisted since the US and Israel launched a war against Iran in February, followed by a ceasefire in April and renewed confrontations between the US and Iran in July.

The developments come amid warnings that Netanyahu could seek to push Washington toward another military confrontation with Tehran.

In an article published Sunday, Haaretz military analyst Amos Harel warned that Netanyahu might resort to military and political escalation to remain in power, using the Iranian issue and pressures surrounding the US midterm elections. Harel also warned against attempts by Netanyahu to persuade Washington to resume military operations despite lacking a domestic mandate to launch another war.

Israeli Channel 12 reported Sunday that Netanyahu had pressed Trump during a phone conversation to resume the war against Iran after the US midterm elections, while the American president preferred to give diplomacy another chance.

The heightened security alert also comes amid political uncertainty in Israel following last week’s parliamentary elections. Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, compared with 48 for opposition parties led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot and 19 for Arab parties.

No bloc secured the 61 seats required to form a government, leaving Israel facing a political deadlock. The results have complicated efforts to form a governing coalition amid disagreements among opposition parties over whether to seek support from Arab parties.

headline: Nine people dead in Learjet crash in south Florida
description: Florida - A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, United States
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Florida - A Learjet crashed on Sunday afternoon in a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board, United States transportation officials said.

The private jet had taken off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to North Eleuthera Airport in the Bahamas, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a statement. Videos on social media showed the jet slamming into the ground next to a road and exploding. “It was a big-time tragedy that happened,” Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said at a press conference near the crash site in Lake Worth Beach. “When you see that video, it’s a jarring thing. It was like a missile coming down, and a massive explosion, debris going everywhere.” The National Transportation Safety Board said it had launched an investigation into the crash, which Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called a “horrific tragedy.”

FAA records list the Bombardier-made Learjet 60’s owner as a Delaware corporation. Canada-based Bombardier said it would fully support the investigation and cooperate as needed. The crash left a “massive crater” by the road near the entrance to a mobile home park, Palm Beach County Commissioner Joel Flores said at the news conference. About 600 people were being evacuated from the area and relocated to two shelters in the county, Flores said.

Heavy rainfall and thunderstorms were occurring in the area at the time, forecaster AccuWeather said in a statement. An audio recording from a Miami air traffic control centre posted on LiveATC, a site that broadcasts air traffic control communications, captured the plane’s final moments before the crash in unusual detail. At first, someone in the plane’s cockpit reported to an air traffic controller that they were “managing the ice” but faced “moderate” turbulence and were seeking “better rides”. Less than a minute later, the person said “Mayday, mayday,” reporting that the plane was suddenly descending at a rate of 10,000 feet per minute.

Seconds later, the person said they were declaring an emergency, with the rate of descent accelerating to 20,000 feet per minute. Less than 20 seconds later, the person said: “We’re going to crash into the ground” before saying that the descent rate had reached 22,000 feet per minute as the plane started banking.

About 35 seconds after the initial mayday announcement, the last thing heard from the cockpit was a rapidly spoken “We’re out of time.”

Flight tracking website Flightradar24 said data showed the vertical descent rate at one point exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.

headline: Jordan’s king calls Israel’s expansionist ambitions ‘biggest threat’ to region’s future
description: Oman - Jordan’s King Abdullah II said on Monday that Israel’s expansionist ambitions pose the greatest threat to the region’s future,
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Oman - Jordan’s King Abdullah II said on Monday that Israel’s expansionist ambitions pose the greatest threat to the region’s future, stressing that regional security and stability cannot be achieved without Palestinians securing their rights to their land.

“Israeli expansionist ambitions remain the greatest threat to the region’s future and its hopes,” Abdullah said in a speech to parliament. He pointed to the continuing humanitarian catastrophe in the Gaza Strip and Israeli attacks in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, despite international calls to halt Israeli violations. He stressed that there could be no security or stability in the region without recognising the Palestinian people’s rights to their land. “Those who believe tyranny grants legitimacy are mistaken, and those who believe time erases the truth are mistaken,” the king said.

He reaffirmed Jordan’s commitment to its principles, Arab identity and defending Arab causes, pledging to maintain that position as his father had before him and his son would after him. The monarch also stressed that achieving a unified Arab position would remain a priority for Jordan.

Israel has waged a genocidal war on Gaza since October 2023, killing more than 74,000 Palestinians and injuring over 175,000 others, most of them women and children.

Israeli military operations and attacks by illegal occupiers have also intensified in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem.

headline: Bangladesh garment workers protesting for higher wages clash with police
description: Dhaka - Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Dhaka - Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than double their current pay, as protests spread across industrial hubs. The South Asian nation of 170 million people is the world’s second-biggest garment exporter behind China, manufacturing clothes for some of the largest international brands.

Hundreds of workers in Gazipur, north of the capital Dhaka, blocked the Dhaka-Tangail highway, vandalising several vehicles, while large groups took to the streets in the Mirpur district, where police dispersed demonstrators with tear gas.

Angry workers also set fire to a police vehicle.

The protests came despite the government’s announcement on Sunday that it would establish a wage board to review the minimum wage in the vital garment industry, which employs millions of people and generates the bulk of Bangladesh’s export earnings.

However, labour leaders say workers’ grievances extend beyond the formation of the board, citing inflation and rising household expenses. The protesters demand a 30,000-taka monthly wage, more than double their current pay. Workers currently earn about 13,000 taka a month, according to Kalpona Akter of the Bangladesh Centre for Workers Solidarity. Police fired stun grenades and tear gas canisters to disperse crowds in Ashulia, a Dhaka suburb and the site of some of the country’s largest factories. “Food prices, cooking gas and electricity bills have all gone up — the government must either bring down the prices of essential commodities or raise our wages,” said Mamum, 28, a factory worker. Machine operator Sharmin, 24, said: “We keep the wheels of the economy turning. They must listen to us.” Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warned that the government was taking strong action to stop the protests.

“Those engaging in unlawful activities and conspiracies under the guise of labour movements will be tackled with an iron hand,” he said after meeting industry leaders on Monday.

However, Ahmed also said earlier Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had instructed officials after hosting an emergency cabinet meeting late on Sunday to “ensure workers’ rights and improve their living standards”.

He said Rahman had told them to make sure production and exports continued “unhindered”.

Bangladesh’s main manufacturer associations for garments and knitwear warned that “prolonged unrest could disrupt production, delay export shipments and affect Bangladesh’s commitments to international buyers”, the state-run BSS news agency said on Monday.

Kamrul Hasan, general secretary of the Ekota Garments Sramik Federation, told news wire some labour leaders had gone into hiding.

headline: Bilal Bin Saqib calls for Pakistan’s active role in shaping future of global finance

author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
LAHORE - Pakistan must move from being a consumer of global financial technologies to becoming an active contributor to the infrastructure, standards and innovation that will define the future of finance, Minister of State and Chairman of the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) Bilal Bin Saqib said at the PBA–LUMS Dialogue on Digital Assets and the Future of Banking.

Speaking during a fireside conversation titled “Partner, Competitor, or Bystander?” with Zafar Masud, Chairman of the Pakistan Banks’ Association and President and CEO of Bank of Punjab, Saqib urged the banking industry to recognise the scale of the transformation taking place across global finance. “Bitcoin was the front door. The bigger transformation is the technology behind it, which is changing how value moves, how financial assets are held and how capital reaches businesses.”

Highlighting developments at JPMorgan, HSBC, Standard Chartered and other international financial institutions, he said digital assets were increasingly being integrated into institutional payments, treasury management and capital markets. “The real opportunity is not giving Pakistanis more assets to trade. It is giving more Pakistanis the opportunity to build assets, businesses and wealth.” Saqib drew attention to the historical development of international banking and payment infrastructure, noting that Pakistan largely became a user of major global financial networks established elsewhere.

He said the emergence of digital assets, tokenisation and artificial intelligence presents Pakistan with an opportunity to participate earlier in the development of new financial capabilities. “When the world’s correspondent banking arrangements and major payment networks were taking shape, Pakistan was largely a user of systems designed elsewhere, rather than an architect of those systems.”

“Today, the rules of finance are evolving again. The question before Pakistan is simple: do we want to keep renting our future, or do we want to help build and own it?” He emphasised that technological independence does not require Pakistan to replicate every international network. “Owning our future does not mean building everything ourselves. It means developing the talent, institutions and technological capabilities to shape the systems we depend upon.”

Discussing Pakistan’s $41.6 billion annual remittance flows, Saqib highlighted the growing importance of reducing the costs associated with international transfers. Saqib said the changing economics have made the search for more efficient financial infrastructure increasingly important for the banking industry. He identified supervised, bank-led payment arrangements involving major Gulf remittance corridors as an opportunity worthy of examination, subject to regulatory coordination and appropriate safeguards. Saqib encouraged bank presidents to establish deeper partnerships with universities, researchers, engineers and emerging technology companies. “The banks of tomorrow should not simply be customers of innovation. They should become launchpads for innovators.”

He suggested that banks could provide Pakistani founders with access to real business problems, technical expertise, mentorship and opportunities to test and demonstrate useful solutions within appropriate safeguards. Saqib also said that artificial intelligence is transforming how financial services are developed, delivered and secured. He pointed to AI’s growing applications in fraud detection, risk management, customer service, software engineering and operational efficiency.

“AI is changing what a small team can build. New financial infrastructure is changing how that team can access customers, capital and global markets. Pakistan must bring these opportunities together.” He urged banking institutions to invest in AI capabilities, develop their existing workforce and strengthen collaboration with universities such as LUMS.

“The greatest opportunity is not simply to use better technology. It is to produce the people who can build that technology.” He also emphasised the importance of coordination between PVARA, the State Bank and other relevant regulatory institutions within their respective statutory mandates. He said the adoption of new technologies must be accompanied by effective supervision, cybersecurity safeguards, consumer protection and institutional accountability.

Looking ahead, Saqib said the next phase of Pakistan’s digital asset journey must be judged by real economic outcomes. “Success is not how many events we hold, how many MoUs we sign or how many announcements we make. Success is how many Pakistani businesses grow, how many financial problems we solve and how much capability we build within our own country.” He concluded with a call for Pakistan to participate actively in shaping the technologies that will influence its economic future.

headline: Six including women, children killed in Hangu house firing
description: PESHAWAR - At least six people, including two women and three childrens were killed in a firing incident inside a house in the Sarokhel area of Hangu district
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: PESHAWAR - At least six people, including two women and three childrens were killed in a firing incident inside a house in the Sarokhel area of Hangu district on Monday. According to District Police Officer (DPO) Salahuddin Kundi, the incident occurred within the jurisdiction of Doaba Police Station, where six people lost their lives in the shooting. The victims included two women, three children and one man. Police shifted the bodies to Doaba Hospital. The DPO said investigations were underway to determine the cause and motive behind the incident. A heavy contingent of police reached the scene soon after receiving information, while a search operation was launched to arrest the suspects.

headline: Fridge cyberattack hits supermarkets across Europe
description: Sjobo, Sweden - A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Sjobo, Sweden - A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.

The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected. “Everything is destroyed,” Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told news wire during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 am (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later. “There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius).”

A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a “limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems”. The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month. While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations.

“It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined,” said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium’s Centre for Cybersecurity, adding she was concerned about the growing number of incidents, in part due to AI.

“All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses — especially by sophisticated actors,” she said. From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarms, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.

At least some of the refrigerator units affected on Monday used temperature control technology from Danish firm Danfoss that was also targeted in the French attack. The firm said it had been working with customers to implement fixes.

The European Commission said the latest incidents highlighted how digital threats are becoming increasingly disruptive.

“They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers’ confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously,” said EU commissioner for agriculture Christophe Hansen. “The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning.”

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops had their ⁠fridge systems attacked.

In Ireland, wholesaler Musgrave said the incident affected systems in 13 of its SuperValu stores, forcing it to remove some chilled and frozen products from sale.

“Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue, and we took immediate action,” it said in a statement. “Our investigation is ongoing.”

Tom Hegel, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, said such attacks were typically linked to extortion, political motives or nation-state operations, with the absence of financial demands in recent cases pointing instead to sabotage.

“Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear,” he said, adding it was hard to trace hackers targeting such systems.

headline: US midterms: Polls show Democrats ahead in battle for Congress
description: Washington - Democrats lead Republicans in national polling ahead of Tuesday’s United States midterm elections, with new surveys showing the party
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
Washington - Democrats lead Republicans in national polling ahead of Tuesday’s United States midterm elections, with new surveys showing the party gaining ground in several closely contested Senate races as voters express dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump’s handling of the economy.

With all 435 House of Representatives seats and 35 Senate seats on the ballot, the elections will determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress for the remaining two years of Trump’s second term. A RealClearPolling average of surveys conducted through October 30 shows Democrats leading Republicans 52% to 43.1% on the generic congressional ballot, an 8.9-percentage-point advantage. An NBC News survey conducted October 28-30 found Democrats ahead 52% to 45%, while an Emerson College poll conducted October 24-26 put the gap at 10 points.

The generic ballot measures nationwide preferences for congressional candidates rather than support in individual districts, meaning a national lead does not necessarily translate into a corresponding number of House seats. Republicans currently control the House, where 218 seats are needed for a majority. The nonpartisan Cook Political Report’s latest ratings, updated Friday, place 222 districts in categories favoring Democrats and 195 favouring Republicans, with another 18 classified as toss-ups. Of the 18 toss-up districts, 14 are currently held by Republicans and four by Democrats.

Cook shifted another 12 House races toward Democrats on October 30, including Republican-held districts in Colorado and Pennsylvania, reflecting changes in its assessment of the electoral landscape. Among the closely watched contests are California’s 22nd District, where Republican Representative David Valadao faces Democrat Randy Villegas; New York’s 17th, where Republican Representative Mike Lawler faces Democrat Cait Conley; and Texas’ 15th, where Republican Representative Monica De La Cruz faces Democrat Bobby Pulido. Republicans are also contesting Democratic-held seats in Florida, North Carolina and Texas, where redistricting has altered the electoral landscape. However, district-level polling remains uneven, and the national figures offer only a broad indication of the environment in which individual races are being fought.

The battle for the Senate is more complicated. Republicans hold 53 seats, compared with 47 held by Democrats and two independents who caucus with them. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to secure a majority. A 50-50 split would leave Republicans in control because Vice President JD Vance can cast tie-breaking votes.

The latest New York Times/Siena University polls, conducted from October 23-November 1, show Democratic candidates ahead in six of seven key Senate battlegrounds and effectively tied with Republicans in the seventh. Five of those Democratic leads are in Republican-held states, including Texas and Kansas, which have not elected Democratic senators since 1988 and 1932, respectively.

In Michigan, the only Democratic-held seat among the seven surveyed, Abdul El-Sayed leads Republican Mike Rogers 53% to 42%, an 11-point advantage.

In Texas, Democrat James Talarico leads Republican Ken Paxton 50% to 43%, while in Maine, Democratic challenger Troy Jackson has 51% support against Republican Senator Susan Collins’ 45%.

Former Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown leads Republican Senator Jon Husted 49% to 44% in Ohio, while Democrat Adam Hamilton leads Republican incumbent Roger Marshall by the same margin in Kansas.

The contests are tighter in Alaska and Iowa. In Alaska, Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan 48% to 46%, while Iowa Democrat Josh Turek is effectively tied with Republican Ashley Hinson, 48% to 47%.

The surveys show Democrats improving their position since September in six of the seven states.

Maine shifted from a three-point Republican lead in September to a six-point Democratic advantage, while Michigan’s Democratic lead widened from five to 11 points. Kansas moved from a tie to a five-point Democratic lead, while Alaska was the only state where Democrats lost ground, with their advantage narrowing from seven points to approximately one point.

The surveys did not include North Carolina, another Republican-held seat where recent polling has consistently shown Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley.

The latest findings are not uniform across pollsters, and several battleground contests remain close in broader polling averages.

The New York Times/Siena surveys found that just 38% of likely voters across the seven battleground states approved of Trump’s job performance. Democratic candidates also led among independent voters in every state surveyed, while respondents expressed greater trust in Democrats on the cost of living, foreign wars and protecting the interests of ordinary people.

Across the seven states, Democratic candidates held a nine-point advantage over Republicans on handling the cost of living.

The findings are consistent with broader national dissatisfaction. An Associated Press-NORC survey conducted on October 8-12 found that 36% of voters approved of Trump’s job performance, while 64% disapproved.

The economy and cost of living emerged as the leading election concerns, cited as important voting issues by 85% and 84% of respondents, respectively. Health care followed at 69%, while 64% identified the war with Iran as an important issue.

The survey also found that 47% of voters wanted Democrats to control the House, compared with 38% who preferred Republicans. For the Senate, the figures were 46% and 38%, respectively.

headline: SC acquits man, upholds life sentence of brother in murder case
description: ISLAMABAD - The Supreme Court has ruled that criminal liability must be established through evidence specific to each accused, observing that one accused
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Supreme Court has ruled that criminal liability must be established through evidence specific to each accused, observing that one accused cannot be convicted merely because the charge against another co-accused has been proved. The apex court acquitted one of two brothers, Shehryar, by extending him the benefit of doubt, while upholding the life imprisonment of his brother, Asfandyar, in a murder case. According to a judgment authored by Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, a three-member bench comprising Justice Muhammad Hashim Khan Kakar, Justice Salahuddin Panhwar and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim partially allowed the criminal appeal after converting a criminal petition into an appeal following arguments on October 21, 2026. According to the case record, the two brothers were accused of shooting dead Kifayatullah in Nowshera Kalan on February 18, 2019. The victim had recorded a statement at the hospital while in an injured condition, while Ejaz Khan was cited as an eyewitness. The trial court had sentenced both accused to life imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs500,000 each on March 19, 2025. The Peshawar High Court upheld their convictions on July 17, 2025. The Supreme Court observed that although the deceased’s statement and the eyewitness implicated both brothers in the shooting, neither established which accused had fired the bullets that caused the fatal injuries. No bullet casings were recovered from the crime scene. The court noted that a repeater gun was recovered on the identification of Shehryar, while a 30-bore pistol was recovered from Asfandyar. The nature of the two bullet wounds found on the deceased’s body was more consistent with shots fired from a 30-bore pistol than a repeater gun. It held that the prosecution had failed to produce sufficiently reliable evidence linking Shehryar to the fatal injuries, making the doubt regarding his involvement impossible to ignore.

However, the court found that direct evidence, medical evidence and recovery of the .30-bore pistol sufficiently established Asfandyar’s involvement in the murder.

Consequently, the Supreme Court set aside Shehryar’s conviction, ordered his immediate release if he was not required in any other case, and dismissed Asfandyar’s appeal, maintaining his life sentence.

headline: Senator Anusha delivers Nawaz’s message at Pak-China governance symposium
description: ISLAMABAD - Senator Anusha Rehman, Additional Secretary General of Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), delivered a congratulatory message on behalf of
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Senator Anusha Rehman, Additional Secretary General of Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N), delivered a congratulatory message on behalf of Muhammad Nawaz Sharif, President PML-N and former Prime Minister of Pakistan, at the Symposium on Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building and China-Pakistan Seminar on Governance, held in Islamabad. In his message, Muhammad Nawaz Sharif extended warm congratulations and greetings to the Communist Party of China (CPC) on the convening of the symposium and welcomed Liu Haixing, Minister of the International Department of the CPC Central Committee, and his delegation to Pakistan. He underscored that Pakistan-China relations enjoy enduring support and a broad-based political consensus across Pakistan, reflecting the strength of the two countries’ all-weather strategic cooperative partnership. He expressed confidence that the visit would further elevate inter-party cooperation to a more strategic level. Highlighting the significance of President Xi Jinping’s vision and Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Muhammad Nawaz Sharif observed that China’s experience offers valuable insights for political parties worldwide in strengthening institutional structures, improving governance, serving the people and promoting sustainable development. He also congratulated the Communist Party of China on the successful convening of the Fifth Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, expressing confidence that its outcomes would further contribute to the party’s progress and institutional development. Referring to the Memorandum of Understanding signed between PML-N and the Communist Party of China in May 2026, he highlighted the importance of institutional cooperation, high-level exchanges, political cadre development, regular inter-party dialogue, sharing of governance experiences and youth leadership development. The message also highlighted PML-N’s development-oriented approach, particularly its contributions to infrastructure development, energy generation and regional connectivity. Muhammad Nawaz Sharif recalled the role of his party’s governments in translating the vision of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) into reality. He expressed confidence that, under the leadership of Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, CPEC Phase II would advance industrialisation, high-tech cooperation, business-to-business partnerships and sustainable economic modernisation.

Emphasising the role of political parties as a bridge between the state and citizens, he noted that exchanges of governance experiences and institutional learning provide valuable opportunities to improve public service delivery and promote prosperity. Concluding his message, Muhammad Nawaz Sharif reaffirmed PML-N’s commitment to further strengthening the longstanding friendship between Pakistan and China and expressed his best wishes for the success of the symposium.

headline: PSX gains 154 points
description: ISLAMABAD - The benchmark KSE 100-index of the PSX witnessed a positive trend on Monday, gaining 154.81 points, a positive change of 0.09 percent, to close at
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The benchmark KSE 100-index of the PSX witnessed a positive trend on Monday, gaining 154.81 points, a positive change of 0.09 percent, to close at 166,564.07 points against 166,409.25 points recorded in the previous trading session. The ready market witnessed a trading volume of 443.432 million shares compared to 825.467 million shares traded in the previous session. The traded value of the ready market reached Rs17.731 billion, down from Rs23.123 billion a day earlier.

Meanwhile, total market capitalisation decreased to Rs18.293 trillion from Rs18.389 trillion recorded in the previous session. Out of 496 companies that traded in the ready market, 137 posted gains, 319 suffered losses, while 40 remained unchanged, reflecting a mixed trend across the overall market. Cnergyico PK led the volume chart with 93.110 million shares, followed by Pervez Ahmed Co with 45.177 million shares, and TPL Properties with 30.105 million shares.

Among the top gainers in the ready market, Pakistan Services Limited surged by Rs98.52 to close at Rs1,083.71, while Pakistan Engineering Company Limited advanced by Rs38.73 to settle at Rs919.02. On the losing side, Unilever Pakistan Foods Limited declined by Rs281.02 to close at Rs25,998.98, while PIA Holding Company LimitedB fell by Rs250.00 to Rs13,700.00.

In the futures (DFC) market, turnover stood at 119.359 million shares with a traded value of Rs4.970 billion, compared with 738.201 million shares worth Rs28.522 billion in the previous session. Of the 316 companies traded in the DFC market, 102 advanced, 212 declined, and 2 remained unchanged.

description: ISLAMABAD - Senate Chairman Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani has warned that any attempt to block, suspend or divert Pakistan’s legitimate share of water would
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Senate Chairman Syed Yousaf Raza Gilani has warned that any attempt to block, suspend or divert Pakistan’s legitimate share of water would constitute an act of war and invite a direct response. He categorically declared that Pakistan would never allow water to be weaponized or used as an instrument of geopolitical pressure, emphasizing that the country’s water security, sovereignty and national interests are non-negotiable. Addressing the Sixth Pakistan Water Week 2026 as Chief Guest, Chairman Senate Gilani asserted that the Indus Waters Treaty remains a binding international agreement and no party can unilaterally alter, suspend or revoke its provisions. He stressed that Pakistan’s position on the Treaty is firm and principled, and any attempt to undermine its rights under the Treaty would have serious consequences. Highlighting the growing challenges confronting Pakistan’s water sector, the Chairman Senate said that the country was facing a dual crisis of catastrophic floods that displace millions of people and prolonged droughts that deplete soil resources and threaten agricultural productivity. At the same time, declining per capita water availability had brought country to a critical threshold, making water security an urgent national priority. Congratulating the International Water Management Institute (IWMI), the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research (CGIAR), the Ministry of Water Resources, the Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) and other development partners, Chairman Senate appreciated their continued efforts in sustaining Pakistan Water Week as an important platform for scientific dialogue, policy development and collaborative solutions to the country’s water challenges. Recalling his experience as Prime Minister during the devastating 2010 floods, which affected approximately 20 million people, Gilani said that he had witnessed first-hand the enormous human cost of natural disasters. Referring also to his engagement with flood-affected communities during the recent floods, he said he had personally witnessed their suffering, heard their accounts and mobilized efforts for relief and rehabilitation. He observed that every major disaster carried lessons that must not be ignored. “Every disaster is a warning we ignored. Disaster response is not resilience, and no single institution can address these challenges in isolation,” he emphasized. The Chairman Senate stressed that Pakistan must move beyond a reactive approach to disaster management and develop a comprehensive framework focused on prevention, preparedness, climate adaptation and long-term resilience. He underscored the need for stronger institutional coordination, enforceable legislation, effective planning and adequate financial allocations for preventive measures. He assured that the Senate would play its constitutional and institutional role in supporting this transition through legislation governing river basins, parliamentary oversight to ensure that water policies deliver tangible benefits to farmers and communities, and advocacy for dedicated budgetary allocations for disaster prevention and water conservation. Emphasizing the importance of water as a unifying factor for the Federation, Chairman Senate Gilani said that equitable water distribution and effective coordination between the federation and provinces were essential for national cohesion. He referred to the 1991 Water Accord and the National Water Policy 2018 as important milestones reflecting the country’s collective commitment to managing its water resources. He stressed that real challenge was effective implementation of these national frameworks, adding that Senate, as House of the Federation, provided an important constitutional forum for strengthening federal-provincial cooperation, building consensus and addressing issues of national significance. Chairman Senate Gilani further observed that Pakistan’s water security was closely linked with its agricultural economy, food security, environmental sustainability and overall economic development. He called for greater investment in water conservation, efficient irrigation systems, modern water management technologies, research and climate-resilient agricultural practices. He emphasized that scientific research, innovation and knowledge-sharing must remain central to policymaking, while partnerships between government institutions, research organizations, academia and international development partners should be strengthened to develop practical and sustainable solutions. Setting a national vision for the future, Chairman Senate Gilani said that Pakistan must emerge as a water-secure and flood-resilient nation by 2047, when the country would celebrate its centenary of independence. He expressed confidence that sustained institutional partnerships, scientific expertise and collective national commitment would enable Pakistan to achieve this ambitious vision. He particularly acknowledged the role of IWMI and its development partners in supporting Pakistan’s efforts to address complex water-related challenges. Concluding his address, Chairman Senate Gilani hoped that the Sixth Pakistan Water Week would produce actionable recommendations, innovative solutions and a clear roadmap for strengthening Pakistan’s water security.

headline: IHC fixes November 5 hearing on plea seeking jail meeting with PTI founder
description: ISLAMABAD - Islamabad High Court (IHC) Monday scheduled for November 5 a petition filed by members of the National Dialogue Committee seeking permission to
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Islamabad High Court (IHC) Monday scheduled for November 5 a petition filed by members of the National Dialogue Committee seeking permission to meet Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) founder Imran Khan at Adiala Jail. Justice Umair Majid Malik will hear the petition along with objections raised by the Registrar’s Office on Thursday. The petition has been filed through senior lawyer Faisal Fareed Chaudhry on behalf of former federal minister Fawad Chaudhry, former Sindh governor Imran Ismail, Mahmood Maulvi and Barrister Saif. The petition names the Secretary of Interior, Secretary of Home Department Punjab and Superintendent of Adiala Jail as respondents. The petitioners stated that, being friends of the PTI founder, they were deeply concerned about his health and well-being. They also expressed serious reservations over the alleged inappropriate behaviour and mistreatment by jail authorities. They further voiced concern over the reported deteriorating health and well-being of Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi. According to the petition, family members, friends and close relatives of the PTI founder had not been allowed to meet him for several months. It stated that restrictions on meetings had fuelled rumours and speculation on social media, contributing to public anxiety and concern. The petitioners said they had approached the court in the interest of political stability, constitutional supremacy and national reconciliation. They contended that restrictions on meetings violated Articles 9 and 14 of the Constitution, relevant prison laws and the United Nations Nelson Mandela Rules. The petition also invoked the Pakistan Prison Rules, 1978, seeking permission for meetings and interviews with the PTI founder in jail. The petitioners have requested the court to direct the Adiala Jail superintendent to arrange a meeting between a National Dialogue Committee delegation and Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi at the prison, with an appropriate time fixed to assess their health, welfare and legal protection.

headline: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
description: UNITED NATIONS - Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging
author: NEWS WIRE
article_text: UNITED NATIONS - Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from the UN cultural organization, UNESCO. “Journalists are increasingly paying with their lives for reporting from the frontlines of war and far too often those responsible for their killings are not held accountable,” said the Director-General of Paris-based UN agency, Khaled El-Enany. UNESCO first began measuring the proportion of journalist killings that go unpunished in 2012. The rate reached 86 per cent in 2024-2025, up one per cent from the previous two-year period. A confirmed total of 189 journalists and other media workers lost their lives in 2024-2025, or 20 per cent more than during the previous biennium and the highest number since 2014-2015. More than two thirds, 127, were killed in conflict zones, accounting for 67 per cent of the death toll. The findings come in the Director-General’s Report on the Safety of Journalists and the Danger of Impunity, which is published every two years to mark the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes against Journalists, observed on 2 November. “Over the past year, at least 34 journalists paid the ultimate price. Six of every seven such killings go unpunished. In conflict settings, the rate of impunity is close to 100 per cent,” UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said in his message for the Day.

headline: Fly Jinnah launches non-stop flights to Abu Dhabi from three Pakistani cities
description: ISLAMABAD - Fly Jinnah, Pakistan’s leading budget carrier, Monday announced the launch of new non-stop flights to Abu Dhabi, expanding its international
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text: ISLAMABAD - Fly Jinnah, Pakistan’s leading budget carrier, Monday announced the launch of new non-stop flights to Abu Dhabi, expanding its international network with services from Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad to the UAE capital. The new services will commence on 28th November, 2026, with five weekly non-stop flights between Karachi and Abu Dhabi. From 1st December, the airline will introduce five weekly flights from Lahore and five weekly flights from Islamabad to Abu Dhabi, bringing the total frequency across the three routes to 15 weekly flights. Commenting on the launch, a Fly Jinnah spokesperson said: “The introduction of our new non-stop services to Abu Dhabi from Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad marks an important step in expanding our international network and strengthening air connectivity between Pakistan and the UAE. By offering direct access to the UAE capital from three major Pakistani cities, we are providing customers with greater travel options while continuing to deliver reliable, value-for-money air travel.” The launch of the new Abu Dhabi services further strengthens Fly Jinnah’s presence in the UAE, complementing its existing non-stop flights between Islamabad and Sharjah, and Lahore and Sharjah, as well as its non-stop service between Lahore and Dubai. The expanded network provides customers with more travel options across the UAE, reinforcing connectivity between the two countries.

headline: PTI rejects claims of internal rift, reaffirms unity behind Imran Khan
description: ISLAMABAD - The political committee of the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Monday dismissed claims of internal divisions or grouping within the
author: Imran Mukhtar
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The political committee of the opposition Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) on Monday dismissed claims of internal divisions or grouping within the party, saying that they remain united behind incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan’s leadership, ideology and mission. “Setting aside political differences, all party leaders and workers will continue their struggle to achieve shared objectives,” said an announcement made by PTI after a meeting of its political committee.

The meeting held a detailed discussion on the overall political situation in the country, the treatment being meted out to PTI chief Imran Khan and his family, the arrests of party leaders and workers, alleged ongoing political victimisation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terrorism and the serious economic challenges facing the public.

The political committee declared the detention of dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, the speaker of the provincial assembly and other parliamentarians illegal and demanded their immediate release. The committee made it clear that detaining elected public representatives is an affront to democratic values and the public mandate. The meeting demanded the immediate and complete implementation of the Supreme Court’s orders regarding the medical treatment of PTI founder Khan. It also demanded that his family be regularly kept informed about his health and that arrangements be made to facilitate family visits. Similarly, appropriate medical facilities and access to family visits must be ensured for Bushra Bibi. The political committee strongly condemned the arrest of Khan’s sisters and the treatment meted out to them.

The political committee strongly condemned the increasing incidents of terrorism across the country, stating that terrorism was a national menace and that effective and serious measures were essential to eliminate it. “Protecting the lives and property of citizens is a fundamental responsibility of the state.” The committee made it clear that counterterrorism operations must not be used as a means of political victimization. Alongside maintaining law and order, the fundamental rights of political workers, members of the public and supporters of opposition political parties must also be protected, it added. The meeting also expressed concern over what it described as exploitation of consumers through excessive LPG prices. The political committee demanded genuine relief for the public through reductions in the prices of petroleum products and electricity. It also called for a reduction in exorbitant electricity bills and the additional financial burden on consumers and demanded that the prices of LPG and other basic necessities be brought within the reach of ordinary citizens.

The meeting emphasized that parliamentarians, the party’s parliamentary group, and other relevant stakeholders must be fully involved in the consultation process. Highlighting the importance of maintaining communication with all stakeholders, the committee stated that the suggestions and concerns of parliamentarians would be given particular consideration in formulating the party’s future course of action.

The political committee stressed that maintaining party discipline was of utmost importance in the current challenging political situation. It decided that disciplinary action would be taken, in accordance with uniform principles, against anyone found violating the party’s established rules, discipline, or policies.

The committee made it clear that irresponsible statements made outside the party platform and violations of organizational discipline would not be overlooked. Compliance with the party’s code of conduct would be ensured to maintain internal unity, solidarity and organizational stability, it added. The participants decided that the party’s future strategy and course of action would be finalised as soon as possible and presented to party workers and the public.

The committee reaffirmed its commitment that, despite the current political pressure, the party would continue its struggle and play an active role in “safeguarding public rights, democracy and the supremacy of the Constitution.”

The meeting held a detailed discussion on the overall political situation in the country, the treatment being meted out to PTI chief Imran Khan and his family, the arrests of party leaders and workers, alleged ongoing political victimisation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, terrorism and the serious economic challenges facing the public.

The political committee declared the detention of dysfunctional KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, the speaker of the provincial assembly and other parliamentarians illegal and demanded their immediate release. The committee made it clear that detaining elected public representatives is an affront to democratic values and the public mandate. The meeting demanded the immediate and complete implementation of the Supreme Court’s orders regarding the medical treatment of PTI founder Khan. It also demanded that his family be regularly kept informed about his health and that arrangements be made to facilitate family visits. Similarly, appropriate medical facilities and access to family visits must be ensured for Bushra Bibi. The political committee strongly condemned the arrest of Khan’s sisters and the treatment meted out to them.

The political committee strongly condemned the increasing incidents of terrorism across the country, stating that terrorism was a national menace and that effective and serious measures were essential to eliminate it. “Protecting the lives and property of citizens is a fundamental responsibility of the state.” The committee made it clear that counterterrorism operations must not be used as a means of political victimization. Alongside maintaining law and order, the fundamental rights of political workers, members of the public and supporters of opposition political parties must also be protected, it added. The meeting also expressed concern over what it described as exploitation of consumers through excessive LPG prices. The political committee demanded genuine relief for the public through reductions in the prices of petroleum products and electricity. It also called for a reduction in exorbitant electricity bills and the additional financial burden on consumers and demanded that the prices of LPG and other basic necessities be brought within the reach of ordinary citizens.

The meeting emphasized that parliamentarians, the party’s parliamentary group, and other relevant stakeholders must be fully involved in the consultation process. Highlighting the importance of maintaining communication with all stakeholders, the committee stated that the suggestions and concerns of parliamentarians would be given particular consideration in formulating the party’s future course of action.

The political committee stressed that maintaining party discipline was of utmost importance in the current challenging political situation. It decided that disciplinary action would be taken, in accordance with uniform principles, against anyone found violating the party’s established rules, discipline, or policies.

The committee made it clear that irresponsible statements made outside the party platform and violations of organizational discipline would not be overlooked. Compliance with the party’s code of conduct would be ensured to maintain internal unity, solidarity and organizational stability, it added. The participants decided that the party’s future strategy and course of action would be finalised as soon as possible and presented to party workers and the public.

The committee reaffirmed its commitment that, despite the current political pressure, the party would continue its struggle and play an active role in “safeguarding public rights, democracy and the supremacy of the Constitution.”
