headline: Deterring Kabul
description: Every now and again, a reminder arrives that the terrorism plaguing Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan is not simply a domestic security challenge, but a
author: The Nation
article_text:
Every now and again, a reminder arrives that the terrorism plaguing Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan is not simply a domestic security challenge, but a conflict sustained by hostile actors across national borders. Pakistan is not merely conducting counterterrorism operations; it is confronting a theatre-level security threat along one of the world’s longest and most fractious frontiers.

The latest exchanges of fire at Torkham and Angoor Adda, including mortar shelling that claimed a civilian life, underscore this dangerous reality. Escalations have already approached the threshold of open war, while border skirmishes, infiltrations and drone attacks have persisted despite repeated diplomatic interventions.

The military’s latest warning to Kabul is therefore both timely and necessary. Pakistan cannot afford illusions about the nature of the threat, particularly when militant organisations allegedly enjoy sanctuary and external sponsorship across the border.

Experience has demonstrated that Kabul responds more readily to credible military deterrence than diplomatic missives. Pakistan’s willingness to impose tangible costs has often produced greater compliance than appeals to reason or neighbourly obligations.

This is not to suggest that diplomacy should be abandoned or escalation pursued for its own sake. Rather, diplomacy must be backed by the unmistakable capacity and resolve to retaliate decisively against cross-border aggression.

Islamabad must maintain constant vigilance, strengthen its border defences and ensure its forces remain prepared for sudden escalation.

Our warnings have been strong, and rightly so. But words alone cannot secure a hostile frontier. The government must ensure that Pakistan’s deterrent remains sufficiently formidable to make further aggression an unacceptable proposition for Kabul.

headline: Over 1,000 police personnel deployed for Rawalpindi polio drive
description: Rawalpindi - More than 1,000 police officers and personnel have been deployed across Rawalpindi to protect polio vaccination teams and ensure the
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Rawalpindi - More than 1,000 police officers and personnel have been deployed across Rawalpindi to protect polio vaccination teams and ensure the smooth conduct of a four-day anti-polio campaign targeting approximately 990,000 children under the age of five in the district.

Rawalpindi Police have finalised a comprehensive security plan for the campaign, which began on Monday, with security cover being provided to 686 vaccination teams and 352 transit points, according to a police spokesperson.

Police station mobile vans, Elite Squad personnel and Dolphin Force teams have also been assigned patrolling duties in their respective jurisdictions to monitor sensitive locations, densely populated areas and public transport hubs.

The spokesperson said police personnel would remain deployed throughout the campaign to ensure the safety of vaccination workers, facilitate their movement and prevent any disruption to the immunisation drive.

Meanwhile, a province-wide anti-polio vaccination campaign targeting more than 9.3 million children under five began in Rawalpindi and 12 other districts of Punjab on Monday. More than 77,000 healthcare workers and polio personnel have been deployed across the province to administer oral vaccine drops and prevent the spread of the crippling disease.

In Rawalpindi, mobile vaccination teams are conducting door-to-door visits to ensure that every eligible child receives the vaccine. A similar vaccination drive has also commenced in neighbouring Murree.

Khalid Pervez, head of the Punjab Anti-Polio Programme, said the campaign in Lahore would continue for seven days, targeting more than 2.28 million children, while the drive in the remaining 12 districts would be completed over four days. More than one million children in Multan and over 1.1 million in Rahim Yar Khan are also scheduled to receive oral polio vaccine drops.

Urging parents to ensure that their children were vaccinated during every campaign, irrespective of the number of doses they had previously received, Khalid Pervez said repeated immunisation was essential to protect children against the disease.

“Polio is an incurable disease, but timely and repeated vaccination is the only way to protect children from lifelong disability,” he said.

He also called on community leaders and religious scholars to raise public awareness about the importance of vaccination and encourage parents to cooperate with field teams. He added that all available resources were being mobilised to reach every targeted child across Punjab.

headline: Asif Rafiq directs PDA to ensure timely completion of uplift schemes
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Local Government, Communications and Works, Agriculture and Housing, Asif Rafiq, has
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Local Government, Communications and Works, Agriculture and Housing, Asif Rafiq, has directed officials of the Peshawar Development Authority (PDA) to ensure the timely completion of ongoing and proposed public development projects in Peshawar and prepare a comprehensive master plan to address urban challenges, particularly traffic-related problems, on a sustainable basis.

He directed the authorities to take immediate and effective measures to address growing traffic pressure, congestion and frequent traffic jams in the city. He further instructed them to formulate practical plans for constructing underpasses and overhead bridges at locations where they are needed, keeping in view actual traffic requirements.

He issued these directives while chairing a meeting in Peshawar on Monday to review progress on various development projects being undertaken by the Peshawar Development Authority. During the meeting, the Director General of PDA gave a detailed briefing on ongoing development projects, the prevailing traffic situation and the city’s future infrastructure requirements.

During the briefing, the authorities presented proposals for the expansion of Hashtnagri Bridge, extension of Faqirabad Bridge up to Government College Chowk, construction of underpasses in Ramdas Bazaar and at Jail Chowk and Shoba Bazaar Chowk. A proposal to introduce an effective traffic management plan at Town Chowk on Khyber Road was also discussed to reduce congestion.

Asif Rafiq said improving traffic flow in Peshawar, providing better commuting facilities to citizens and aligning development projects with modern urban requirements were among the government’s key priorities.

He directed the authorities to conduct technical and practical assessments of all proposed projects and determine their priorities to ensure sustainable solutions to public problems.

He also directed the Peshawar Development Authority to play an active role in enhancing the city’s beauty. He emphasised that, alongside improving commuting facilities near the Motorway and along GT Road, special attention should be given to plantation and the cultivation of flowers to transform Peshawar into a clean, green and attractive city.

The Adviser particularly stressed the need for effective measures to improve traffic flow on Khyber Road, eliminate congestion and reduce commuting difficulties faced by citizens.

He said public needs must remain the foremost priority in the planning and execution of all development projects.

headline: Traders allege PERA high-handedness in Hassanabdal
description: Attock - Traders in Hassanabdal have accused officials of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (PERA) of abusing their powers, harassing
author: Muhammad Sabrin
article_text:
Attock - Traders in Hassanabdal have accused officials of the Punjab Enforcement and Regulatory Authority (PERA) of abusing their powers, harassing small shopkeepers and confiscating merchandise from inside shops during an anti-encroachment drive, allegedly without following prescribed legal procedures.

Speaking to newsmen on Monday, the general secretary of the Traders Association and other shopkeepers alleged that PERA officials were visiting markets and bazaars under the pretext of removing encroachments but were instead humiliating traders, threatening them with legal action and imposing heavy fines. They said several shopkeepers had been unnecessarily pressured, threatened with proceedings and summoned to government offices, creating an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty among the local business community.

The traders further alleged that officials resorted to registering what they described as false cases against those who questioned their conduct or challenged their authority. They claimed that merchandise was being seized even from inside shops and commercial premises without issuing seizure receipts, recovery memos or written explanations.

With Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif expected to visit the area on Tuesday, traders alleged that PERA officials had intensified their enforcement activities and were confiscating goods from inside shops to demonstrate their performance ahead of the visit. In this connection, a CCTV video circulated on social media on Monday, reportedly showing a PERA official removing merchandise from a shop and loading it into an official vehicle.

The incident has fuelled resentment among traders, who have questioned the authority of enforcement personnel to enter commercial premises and remove goods without following the prescribed legal procedures.

The business community maintained that it supported lawful action against illegal encroachments and measures to improve traffic flow and cleanliness. However, it emphasised that such operations should not become a pretext for intimidation, arbitrary confiscation of property or selective enforcement.

The traders also accused PERA officials of targeting small shopkeepers while allegedly overlooking permanent structures and concrete encroachments. They called on senior PERA authorities and the district administration to order an impartial inquiry into the allegations, establish the legal grounds for confiscating merchandise from inside shops and take disciplinary action against any official found guilty of abusing authority.

It may be recalled that a few weeks ago, PERA officials booked five nominated and 35 unidentified shopkeepers of Sarafa Bazaar under Sections 186, 353, 354, 503 and 509 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) for allegedly resisting an anti-encroachment operation. Subsequently, the Tehsil Bar Association observed a complete strike in protest against what it described as the registration of a false case against members of the local trading community.

Meanwhile, citizens have questioned whether the intensified enforcement activity is intended to project the authority’s performance ahead of the chief minister’s visit and that of other senior government officials, rather than ensure the transparent and impartial removal of encroachments. However, this allegation could not be independently verified.

Concerns have also been raised over alleged traffic violations by some PERA personnel. Citizens claimed that certain officials had been seen riding motorcycles without helmets and, on some occasions, carrying three people on a single motorcycle. They questioned whether enforcement personnel were themselves complying with traffic regulations while imposing restrictions and penalties on ordinary commuters.

When contacted, district PERA officials said the anti-encroachment operation was being conducted in accordance with the law to remove illegal encroachments and facilitate the public. They denied that traders were being victimised.

headline: KP Governor calls for digital reforms to promote investment in province
description: Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Monday stressed the need to promote business activities in the province through a
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi on Monday stressed the need to promote business activities in the province through a transparent, efficient and digital governance system, saying that providing maximum facilities to the business community should remain a key government priority.

Chairing a meeting on ease of doing business and proposed reforms in relevant laws and regulations, the Governor said unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles should be eliminated through the introduction of modern digital systems, enabling entrepreneurs to access government services without having to make repeated visits to public offices.

The meeting was attended by Adviser to the Governor on Finance Tariq Mahmood, Adviser on Industries Irshad Ahmad, Adviser on Planning and Development Usman Saifullah, Chief Secretary Dr Fakhare Alam Irfan, the Secretary Industries and other senior officials.

The participants briefed the Governor on measures aimed at facilitating businesses, the issuance of no-objection certificates (NoCs), implementation of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Asaan Karobar Act 2025, the Asaan Karobar Live Portal, digitisation of regulatory licensing and certification offices, and steps taken to address existing challenges.

The meeting was also informed about reform proposals prepared in consultation with 19 government departments.

The Governor directed the authorities to introduce a single-window system to provide all business-related services under one roof and further simplify the online registration process to encourage investment and improve public convenience.

He said an effective mechanism should be developed to ensure that citizens are not required to visit government offices for routine matters. He also instructed the authorities to activate the Asaan Karobar online complaints portal at the earliest to ensure the prompt resolution of issues faced by the business community.

Governor Kundi directed appointment of a focal person for effective coordination with the federal government and called for an immediate meeting with the Information Technology Department to expedite the implementation of digital reforms.

He also ordered that a meeting of the committee formed for Asaan Karobar be convened soon to initiate the practical implementation of the proposed reforms.

He said linking public services with a transparent, efficient and modern digital system was the need of the hour to promote business activities, encourage investment and improve service delivery across the province.

headline: Wounded robber held after armed encounter, two accomplices escape
description: Rawalpindi - Sadar Berooni police on Monday claimed to have arrested an alleged robber after he was wounded in an armed encounter with a police
author: Mudassir Raja
article_text:
Rawalpindi - Sadar Berooni police on Monday claimed to have arrested an alleged robber after he was wounded in an armed encounter with a police team, while his two accomplices managed to escape under the cover of darkness on Sunday night.

According to the first information report (FIR), a police team had been deployed on Terbela Colony Road for routine patrolling and checking at around 10.10pm on Sunday when officers spotted three men riding a motorcycle towards them from Dhoke Imam Din Chowk.

When the policemen signalled the motorcyclists to stop, the suspects allegedly attempted to turn back abruptly but lost control of their motorcycle. They then pulled out pistols and opened fire directly at the police party, forcing the officers to take cover behind their official vehicle.

The police said the suspects ignored repeated calls to surrender and instead attempted to flee while continuing to fire at the law enforcers. The police party resorted to aerial firing in self-defence, according to the FIR.

After the exchange of fire subsided, the police found one of the suspects lying wounded at the scene. He identified himself as Umer bin Tariq alias Peru, a resident of Mumtaz Market, Adiala Road. A pistol loaded with live ammunition was allegedly recovered from his possession.

During initial interrogation, the arrested suspect identified his two fleeing accomplices as Jahanzeb Khan, a resident of Dheri Hassanabad, and Subhan Ullah, a resident of Mumtaz Market, Adiala Road, the police said.

The police also took into custody the abandoned motorcycle, which had allegedly been snatched at gunpoint on October 26 within the jurisdiction of Sadar Berooni police station.

The wounded suspect was shifted to Benazir Bhutto Hospital for medical examination and treatment. Police registered a case under charges relating to attempted murder, an armed attack on the police, damage to a police vehicle and rioting, according to the FIR.

Rickshaw driver shoots food vendor dead

A roadside food vendor was shot dead allegedly by a rickshaw driver following a dispute over parking in Raza Plaza Chowk within the jurisdiction of Chaklala police station on Sunday evening.

According to the first information report (FIR), lodged by Muhammad Zaheer, the victim’s brother, he was present at the chowk along with other relatives when the incident occurred. His brother, Hafeez Akhtar, operated a roadside barbecue stall at the location every evening, selling tikka to customers.

The complainant told police that Hafeez had asked Shahid Nazeer, a rickshaw driver, not to park his three-wheeler in front of the food stall, as it was obstructing access to the business. The request allegedly infuriated Shahid, who pulled out a pistol and shot Hafeez in the chest before fleeing the scene, leaving his rickshaw behind, according to the FIR. The police registered a case against the nominated suspect and initiated an investigation into the incident.

Rawalpindi - Sadar Berooni police on Monday claimed to have arrested an alleged robber after he was wounded in an armed encounter with a police team, while his two accomplices managed to escape under the cover of darkness on Sunday night.

According to the first information report (FIR), a police team had been deployed on Terbela Colony Road for routine patrolling and checking at around 10.10pm on Sunday when officers spotted three men riding a motorcycle towards them from Dhoke Imam Din Chowk.

When the policemen signalled the motorcyclists to stop, the suspects allegedly attempted to turn back abruptly but lost control of their motorcycle. They then pulled out pistols and opened fire directly at the police party, forcing the officers to take cover behind their official vehicle.

The police said the suspects ignored repeated calls to surrender and instead attempted to flee while continuing to fire at the law enforcers. The police party resorted to aerial firing in self-defence, according to the FIR.

After the exchange of fire subsided, the police found one of the suspects lying wounded at the scene. He identified himself as Umer bin Tariq alias Peru, a resident of Mumtaz Market, Adiala Road. A pistol loaded with live ammunition was allegedly recovered from his possession.

During initial interrogation, the arrested suspect identified his two fleeing accomplices as Jahanzeb Khan, a resident of Dheri Hassanabad, and Subhan Ullah, a resident of Mumtaz Market, Adiala Road, the police said.

The police also took into custody the abandoned motorcycle, which had allegedly been snatched at gunpoint on October 26 within the jurisdiction of Sadar Berooni police station.

The wounded suspect was shifted to Benazir Bhutto Hospital for medical examination and treatment. Police registered a case under charges relating to attempted murder, an armed attack on the police, damage to a police vehicle and rioting, according to the FIR.

Rickshaw driver shoots food vendor dead

A roadside food vendor was shot dead allegedly by a rickshaw driver following a dispute over parking in Raza Plaza Chowk within the jurisdiction of Chaklala police station on Sunday evening.

According to the first information report (FIR), lodged by Muhammad Zaheer, the victim’s brother, he was present at the chowk along with other relatives when the incident occurred. His brother, Hafeez Akhtar, operated a roadside barbecue stall at the location every evening, selling tikka to customers.

The complainant told police that Hafeez had asked Shahid Nazeer, a rickshaw driver, not to park his three-wheeler in front of the food stall, as it was obstructing access to the business. The request allegedly infuriated Shahid, who pulled out a pistol and shot Hafeez in the chest before fleeing the scene, leaving his rickshaw behind, according to the FIR. The police registered a case against the nominated suspect and initiated an investigation into the incident.

headline: Amir Javed directs KP Labour Dept to focus on effective public service delivery
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Law, Labour and Inter-Provincial Coordination, Amir Javed, has directed the Labour
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Law, Labour and Inter-Provincial Coordination, Amir Javed, has directed the Labour Department to focus on effective public service delivery, transparency and improved field performance, stressing that existing systems should be made functional rather than introducing unnecessary new initiatives.

Chairing an introductory meeting of the Labour Department, the Adviser called for comprehensive details of 108,000 registered workers, including their registration records, digital data, departmental receipts and measures taken to safeguard labour rights. He also directed the department to strengthen labour courts, ensure the implementation of minimum wages, curb child labour and promote industrial peace. Emphasising the practical enforcement of labour laws, Amir Javed said the protection of workers’ rights must go beyond paperwork and produce tangible results. He directed the establishment of effective coordination between administrative magistrates and Labour Department inspectors, while also calling for stronger mechanisms to resolve industrial disputes through mediation.

The Adviser sought complete details of pending cases before labour courts, including their nature and current status, within 24 hours. He also directed the department to deploy more personnel in the field instead of concentrating excessive staff in offices, ensuring their direct involvement in resolving workers’ issues and improving service delivery.

He further called for 100 per cent attendance across all sections of the department, including field staff, and directed the authorities to assign additional responsibilities wherever necessary and undertake administrative adjustments to improve institutional efficiency.

Amir Javed made it clear that future recruitment would only be undertaken after proper workforce planning and identification of essential vacant positions. He also sought details of all sanctioned, filled and vacant posts, ranging from senior-level positions to Class-IV employees.

The meeting was also briefed on 37 labour colonies, 7,700 residential flats and 45 schools. The Adviser sought complete records regarding the allocation of residential flats, along with details of 1,664 teachers and their performance.

Furthermore, he directed that the human rights-related wings of the Labour Department be linked with the proposed joint referral mechanism and digital portal of the Directorate General of Law and Human Rights. The initiative aims to streamline complaint registration, referrals to relevant institutions and the timely resolution of grievances.

The Adviser stressed that the department’s performance would ultimately be judged not by office procedures but by the tangible relief provided to workers, protection of their rights and effective delivery of public services.

headline: Samar Bilour expresses concern over financial irregularities in KP audit report
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations, Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon Bilour, has expressed serious concern over revelations of billions of rupees in financial irregularities and accounting discrepancies in the provincial financial system, as highlighted in the Audit Report for Fiscal Year 2024-25.

She said the inability to fully verify billions of rupees in expenditures from the provincial exchequer during the PTI government was a matter of grave concern.

In a statement, she said that, according to the audit report, government expenditures amounting to Rs72.46 billion could not be fully verified, while additional entries amounting to Rs104.26 billion were also recorded beyond the budget approved by the Provincial Assembly. She stressed that these discrepancies required clear and satisfactory explanations.

Samar Bilour said the report had also identified Rs153.68 billion in development expenditures incorrectly recorded under various accounting heads, along with a negative balance of Rs39.58 billion in the Public Account. These findings, she said, raised serious questions about financial discipline, transparency and accountability.

She pointed out that accounting records of external loans amounting to Rs98.89 billion were incomplete, while payments of Rs51.85 billion against foreign loans and interest could not be fully verified. Similarly, the failure to update records of provincial domestic loans since 2017-18 and loans obtained from the federal government since 2013-14 pointed to significant weaknesses in the financial monitoring system.

She said that, in addition to additional entries amounting to Rs20.20 billion in the development budget, further additional entries worth billions of rupees had also been identified in the budgets of key departments, including Health, Education, Police and Highways. She emphasised that the reasons for these entries, along with their legal and financial justifications, must be clearly established.

Samar Bilour said that every rupee collected through public taxes was a public trust and that those entrusted with managing public funds must provide a complete account of their utilisation.

She called for a transparent and impartial examination of all audit objections, emphasising that wherever irregularities were established, responsibility must be fixed and accountability ensured.

She stressed that safeguarding public resources, ensuring financial transparency and strengthening institutional accountability were fundamental requirements of responsible governance and that no compromise should be made on these principles.

Samar assumes charge of KP Relief, Rehabilitation Dept

Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Information and Public Relations and Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement, Samar Haroon Bilour, has formally assumed charge of the Department of Relief, Rehabilitation and Settlement.

On the occasion, she expressed her gratitude to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa for reposing confidence in her and entrusting her with this important responsibility. She described the trust placed in her as an honour and pledged to discharge her duties with dedication, commitment and sincerity.

In a statement, Samar Bilour said that building a progressive, developed and stronger Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was a shared vision. She emphasised that the reconstruction of the province, rehabilitation of affected communities and prompt resolution of public grievances would remain her foremost priorities.

She noted that climate change, terrorism and recurring natural disasters had created serious challenges for the province, making comprehensive and timely rehabilitation measures imperative.

She assured that immediate relief would be provided to people affected by disasters, tragedies or emergencies across the province, with all available resources mobilised to address their needs.

The Adviser further stated that practical measures would be taken to ensure the timely rehabilitation and resettlement of families affected by natural disasters and other calamities, enabling them to overcome their difficulties and return to normal life as soon as possible.

headline: Rescue 1122 Shangla responds to 327 emergencies in October
description: Shangla - Rescue 1122 Shangla has released its monthly performance report for October, revealing that the emergency service responded to 327
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
Shangla - Rescue 1122 Shangla has released its monthly performance report for October, revealing that the emergency service responded to 327 emergencies across the mountainous district during the month. Meanwhile, under its Hospital Referral Service, 158 patients were shifted from various hospitals in Shangla to teaching hospitals for advanced medical treatment.

According to the detailed monthly report issued by the district office of Rescue 1122, rescue personnel remained fully active and alert throughout October, carrying out relief and rescue operations in response to road traffic accidents, medical emergencies, fire incidents and other untoward situations in different parts of the district.

The report revealed that during October, Rescue 1122 responded to seven road traffic accidents, 147 medical emergencies and two fire incidents. In addition, rescue teams carried out recovery operations and retrieved 12 vehicles involved in different accidents across the district. These operations reflect the wide-ranging responsibilities performed by Rescue 1122 in the challenging mountainous terrain of Shangla.

Sharing details, District Emergency Officer Rescue 1122 Shangla, Engineer Malik Sher Dil Khan, said rescue personnel performed their professional duties with utmost dedication, commitment and promptness throughout October.

He said that whenever an accident or medical emergency was reported from any part of the district, Rescue 1122 teams immediately rushed to the scene, provided first aid to the injured and shifted them to nearby hospitals.

He said road traffic accidents in Shangla were often serious due to the difficult terrain, narrow roads and sharp turns.

Similarly, he said medical emergencies accounted for the largest share of cases handled during the month. Rescue 1122 responded to 147 medical emergencies, including cardiac problems, respiratory complications, maternity emergencies and other critical conditions requiring immediate med ical assistance and transportation to hospitals.

The timely provision of first aid and transportation to hospitals in such cases is vital for saving lives, he added.

The report also mentioned two fire incidents during the month, in which Rescue 1122 teams responded promptly and carried out firefighting and rescue operations, preventing further loss of life and property.

Another significant aspect of the October performance was the Hospital Referral Service, which serves as a lifeline for patients in remote districts such as Shangla. Under this service, a total of 158 patients were shifted from various hospitals in Shangla to teaching hospitals, including Saidu Teaching Hospital Swat, Ayub Teaching Hospital Abbottabad and other tertiary care facilities, for specialised treatment and better medical care.

Apart from emergency response activities, the report also highlighted the misuse of the emergency helpline. During October, the Rescue 1122 Shangla Control Room received a total of 12,980 calls. Of these, only 327 were genuine emergency calls, while 10,883 were classified as unnecessary or irrelevant calls and 1,928 were recorded as dropped calls.

The high number of unnecessary calls creates difficulties in the smooth functioning of the emergency service and wastes the valuable time of control room staff.

The District Emergency Officer appealed to the general public to use the emergency helpline 1122 responsibly and only in genuine emergencies so that assistance could reach those in need without delay.

The October performance report highlights the role of Rescue 1122 Shangla in saving lives and providing emergency assistance to people in distress across the remote and mountainous district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

headline: Performance of digitised arms licensing system reviewed
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Home and Tribal Affairs, Food and Women Empowerment, Kifayat Ullah Khan, has reviewed
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Home and Tribal Affairs, Food and Women Empowerment, Kifayat Ullah Khan, has reviewed the performance of the digitised arms licensing system operating through the Dastak App, stressing the need for further improvements in service delivery, transparency, accountability and timely processing of applications.

The Adviser was briefed by Section Officer (Arms) Faiz Muhammad at the Adviser’s Office at 3:00pm on the performance of the Dastak App from February 2024 to October 2026. The briefing covered revenue generation, licences issued, licence cards printed and the status of pending applications.

The briefing revealed that the digitised system had generated online revenue exceeding Rs4.39 billion, while more than 381,800 arms licences had been issued and over 380,000 licence cards printed. The system has significantly reduced manual procedures through the introduction of online applications, digital payments, biometric authentication and electronic verification.

The Adviser appreciated the introduction of the digital licensing mechanism, describing it as an important step towards improving transparency, strengthening institutional accountability and facilitating citizens through technology-based public services. Taking notice of pending applications, particularly those awaiting biometric, police and departmental verification, the Adviser stressed the need for coordinated efforts among all relevant departments to expedite the verification process and ensure the timely disposal of applications.

He directed the concerned authorities to take up the issue of pending verifications with the relevant departments, particularly those with a large number of outstanding cases, and establish an effective coordination mechanism to prevent unnecessary delays.

The Adviser stressed that applicants should be properly guided on completing biometric verification through PakID/NADRA to ensure that applications are not unnecessarily delayed at different stages of processing.

He underscored the importance of maintaining a transparent, efficient and citizen-friendly system, directing the concerned officials to regularly monitor the progress of applications, identify bottlenecks and take corrective measures to ensure timely service delivery.

The Adviser also emphasised that the digital system should ensure proper record management, accurate revenue tracking and effective monitoring of arms licensing procedures while maintaining all prescribed legal and security requirements.

He directed the concerned officials to submit regular progress reports on pending cases, departmental verification and the overall performance of the Dastak App to ensure that the system continues to provide maximum facilitation to the public.

The Adviser reiterated that modern technology must translate into practical relief for citizens, greater institutional transparency and efficient governance.

headline: Telemedicine network to expand with 10 additional centres
description: ISLAMABAD - The Ministry of National Health Services has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Sehat Kahani to expand telemedicine
author: Farwa Naqvi
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Ministry of National Health Services has signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Sehat Kahani to expand telemedicine services in the country, with 10 additional centres planned under the second phase of the initiative. Announcing the launch of the new phase at the MoU signing ceremony, Federal Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said the expansion followed the completion of the first phase, during which 10 telemedicine centres had been established.

He said 500 additional doctors had been brought into the telemedicine network, with Sehat Kahani bearing their consultation-related costs. The initiative, he added, had already helped citizens save approximately Rs70 million in healthcare expenses.

The minister said the government was using modern technology to improve access to healthcare, strengthen primary healthcare services and reduce the growing burden on major hospitals. He stressed that telemedicine could play an important role in extending medical consultations to people who faced difficulties accessing conventional healthcare facilities.

Separately, Mustafa Kamal announced that the existing emergency department at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) would be shifted to the hospital’s new emergency facility within the next few days. A state-of-the-art telemedicine centre would subsequently be established at the site of the old emergency department, he added.

Reaffirming the government’s commitment to universal healthcare, the minister said health-sector reforms were progressing to improve the availability and quality of medical services, particularly for people unable to afford expensive healthcare.

He said the expansion of technology-enabled healthcare services was part of broader efforts to make medical consultations more accessible and strengthen the country’s primary healthcare system.

headline: Sherry Rehman warns of mounting global challenges
description: ISLAMABAD - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman has called for climate justice, renewable energy, responsible
author: SHAFQAT ALI
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman has called for climate justice, renewable energy, responsible artificial intelligence and balanced diplomacy, warning that the world is entering an era marked by uncertainty, resource scarcity and technological transformation.

Addressing the 29th Sustainable Development Conference organised by the Sustainable Development Policy Institute (SDPI), she said climate change was among the most serious challenges confronting the world, with Pakistan increasingly exposed to extreme weather events and environmental disasters. Recalling the devastating floods that submerged one-third of the country, she said the time available for recovery and rehabilitation was shrinking as climate-related disasters became more frequent.

Highlighting the need for climate justice, she stressed that vulnerable countries must receive adequate financing, resources and international cooperation to cope with the consequences of environmental degradation. She also cited smog in Lahore as an indication of the growing public health costs of environmental pollution.

Turning to technological change, Sherry Rehman said artificial intelligence was no longer merely an auxiliary tool but had become integral to businesses and public systems. However, she cautioned that its expanding use carried environmental costs, particularly through the energy and water consumption of data centres and supercomputing infrastructure. She also warned that technological progress did not necessarily guarantee equal opportunities for all sections of society.

On energy security, she said the world’s dependence on fossil fuels needed to be reduced, noting that global fossil fuel subsidies amounted to approximately $7 trillion annually.

Pakistan’s energy difficulties, she maintained, were compounded by an outdated and inefficient electricity system.

She described the rapid adoption of solar power in Pakistan as an encouraging development, arguing that renewable and decentralised energy systems would shape the future.

She also identified battery technology and energy storage as critical to strengthening energy security, while calling for charging infrastructure and incentives to promote electric motorcycles, three-wheelers and other cleaner transport options.

Referring to international affairs, the PPP leader said geopolitical tensions had slowed progress towards climate commitments, making sustainable development and efficient resource management increasingly important. She said Pakistan was navigating a multipolar world through balanced diplomacy and emphasised the need for Western Asia to develop its own regional security arrangements.

She maintained that Pakistan, despite its substantial economic and environmental challenges, had demonstrated resilience through indigenous solutions and growing investment in renewable energy, positioning itself as a potential contributor to solutions to global challenges.

headline: MIH observes infection prevention week
description: ISLAMABAD - Maroof International Hospital (MIH) has observed infection prevention and control week to promote safe healthcare practices and strengthen
author: APP
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Maroof International Hospital (MIH) has observed infection prevention and control week to promote safe healthcare practices and strengthen adherence to infection prevention protocols across its departments. During the week, departmental rounds were conducted to review infection prevention practices, assess compliance with safety protocols and encourage a culture of responsibility to protect patients, healthcare professionals and visitors.

A special recognition ceremony was also organized at the conclusion of the week to acknowledge departments demonstrating outstanding commitment and vigilance in maintaining infection prevention and control standards.

The Intensive Care Unit (ICU) secured first position, followed by the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and Labour Room, which jointly achieved second position. The Dialysis Department secured third position.

The hospital appreciated the efforts of all participating teams, recognizing their teamwork, discipline and commitment to maintaining safe clinical practices.

The initiative highlighted the importance of consistent infection prevention measures in improving patient safety and ensuring quality healthcare services.

headline: BISE Rawalpindi to begin HSSC second annual exams today
description: RAWALPINDI - The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE), Rawalpindi, has finalised arrangements for the Higher Secondary School Certificate
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
RAWALPINDI - The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE), Rawalpindi, has finalised arrangements for the Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC) Second Annual Examination 2026, which is scheduled to commence on Tuesday (today).

According to a press release issued by the Board’s spokesman, roll number slips have been issued to all candidates, while the necessary supervisory staff has been deployed at examination centres across the region.

A total of 41 examination centres have been established across the Board’s jurisdiction, including 17 in Rawalpindi district, seven in Attock, five in Jhelum, four in Chakwal, two in Talagang and two in Murree. Of the total centres, 11 have been designated for male candidates, 12 for female candidates and 17 as combined examination centres.

To ensure transparency and prevent unfair examination practices, all designated examination centres have been connected to a central Command and Control Centre for real-time online monitoring. Closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras have also been installed at all centres to strengthen surveillance and oversight.

Preparations for the examinations were reviewed at a high-level meeting chaired by BISE Rawalpindi Chairman Prof Dr Iqbal Mahmood. Controller of Examinations Mubashir Saeed and Board Secretary Zualkaif Umar Shah also attended the meeting.

Addressing the meeting, Prof Dr Iqbal Mahmood said the examinations were being conducted in accordance with the vision of Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, the directives of Punjab Education Minister Rana Sikandar Hayat and the government’s prescribed standard operating procedures (SOPs). He stressed that the Board would not compromise on merit, transparency or discipline during the examination process.

Controller of Examinations Mubashir Saeed informed the meeting that mobile inspectors, district vigilance committees and inspection teams would conduct regular visits to examination centres. The teams would submit field reports to the Board to facilitate prompt action against any administrative shortcomings or irregularities.

Board Secretary Zualkaif Umar Shah said arrangements had also been finalised for the secure transportation of question papers to examination centres and the safe return of answer scripts to the Board’s office.

headline: NUMS to issue provisional merit list on Dec 10
description: ISLAMABAD - The National University of Medical Sciences (NUMS) is scheduled to announce the provisional merit list for MBBS and BDS admissions for the 2026-27
author: APP
article_text: ISLAMABAD - The National University of Medical Sciences (NUMS) is scheduled to announce the provisional merit list for MBBS and BDS admissions for the 2026-27 academic session on December 10, 2026. According to the admission schedule, the first selection list for MBBS will be announced on December 17, 2026, while the first selection list for BDS is scheduled for January 21, 2027. Applicants have been advised to note that the provisional merit list and selection lists are separate stages of the admission process and to follow all official updates to avoid missing important deadlines. Students seeking admission through NUMS have been advised to regularly check admission-related announcements, including merit lists, college-wise merit details and fee structures, through the university’s official channels.

headline: Students shifted from 143 Rawalpindi school buildings declared unsafe
description: Rawalpindi - As many as 143 school buildings in Rawalpindi have been identified as completely unsafe or partially damaged in a district-wide safety
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
Rawalpindi - As many as 143 school buildings in Rawalpindi have been identified as completely unsafe or partially damaged in a district-wide safety survey, prompting the education authorities to relocate students to nearby schools and arrange evening shifts in safe premises to ensure that their education is not disrupted.

The survey covered more than 8,300 government and private schools across the district, with most of the buildings identified as unsafe reportedly located in the old city areas of Rawalpindi. Many of these structures are either very old or have not undergone proper repair and maintenance for an extended period.

The building safety audit was launched across Punjab following the collapse of a private school building in Peshawar last month, which reportedly claimed the lives of 34 students and a teacher.

In Rawalpindi, the District Education Authority (DEA) constituted 47 inspection teams comprising representatives of Rescue 1122, the relevant municipal authorities, the Education Department and civil engineers from the district administration to assess the structural condition of school buildings.

The teams inspected approximately 1,300 government schools and 7,000 private schools, identifying 143 buildings as either completely unsafe or partially damaged. The reported extent of damage to the affected structures ranged from 20 to 80 per cent.

Following the findings, the education authorities began relocating students from buildings considered unsafe. Depending on the condition of the premises, students were either shifted to nearby schools or accommodated in safe classrooms within the same buildings. Talking to The Nation, Chief Executive Officer of the District Education Authority Yasin Baloch said arrangements had been made to ensure the safety of students and the continuation of academic activities.

He said the number of buildings declared completely unsafe was relatively small, adding that students studying in such structures had been shifted to nearby schools within a radius of one to two kilometres. Evening shifts had also been introduced in suitable school buildings to accommodate the relocated students, he added.

The CEO said inspection teams had also identified several buildings in which only certain rooms or portions had been declared unsafe. In such cases, the authorities had closed the affected sections and shifted students to classrooms considered structurally safe.

He added that evening shifts had also been introduced in partially damaged school buildings where safe classrooms were available, allowing educational activities to continue without exposing students to potential risks.

Yasin Baloch further said the Communications and Works Department had initiated repair and maintenance work in buildings requiring remedial measures.

The work was expected to be completed soon, he added.

Regarding private educational institutions, the CEO said no major structural damage had been reported in the district’s private schools. However, inspection teams had identified certain buildings requiring repair and maintenance, following which notices had been issued to the respective school administrations to complete the necessary work without delay.

The building safety audit was launched across Punjab following the collapse of a private school building in Peshawar last month, which reportedly claimed the lives of 34 students and a teacher.

Depending on the condition of the premises, students were either shifted to nearby schools or accommodated in safe classrooms within the same buildings. headline: Power Division official calls for customer facilitation centres across DISCOs
description: ISLAMABAD - A senior official of the Ministry of Energy’s Power Division has called for the establishment of customer facilitation centres across
author: PR
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A senior official of the Ministry of Energy’s Power Division has called for the establishment of customer facilitation centres across all power distribution companies (DISCOs), describing the initiative as an effective way to address consumers’ electricity-related complaints under one roof.

Khalid Khan, Joint Secretary (CA&D) at the Power Division, made the remarks during a visit to the Regional Customer Facilitation Centre established at the Islamabad Electric Supply Company (IESCO) headquarters.

IESCO Chairman Dr Tahir Masood, Chief Executive Officer Engr Chaudhry Khalid Mahmood and other senior officials received him on arrival.

During the visit, Dr Masood briefed the visiting official on the company’s efforts to improve customer services in line with the Prime Minister’s vision and the directives of the Minister for Energy. He said IESCO was committed to providing consumers with efficient and timely services through its customer facilitation centres.

He explained that the centres provided a single-window facility for addressing a range of consumer complaints and service-related matters, including requests for instalment of electricity bills, correction of billing errors, extensions in payment deadlines and complaints about power outages.

Applications for new electricity connections were also being processed at the centres.

Appreciating the initiative, Khalid Khan commended IESCO’s board of directors and management for adopting a customer-friendly approach. He stressed the need to establish similar centres in other DISCOs to enable consumers to resolve their electricity-related issues conveniently and without unnecessary difficulty.

headline: Gang accused of misusing fingerprints to activate illegal SIMs busted
description: ISLAMABAD - A gang allegedly exploiting people’s biometric fingerprints to activate multiple mobile phone SIM cards without their knowledge
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - A gang allegedly exploiting people’s biometric fingerprints to activate multiple mobile phone SIM cards without their knowledge has been busted by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), with four suspects arrested in connection with the racket.

According to investigators, the suspects approached unsuspecting people at different locations and offered them free SIM cards. After obtaining their thumb impressions on biometric verification devices, they allegedly claimed that the scans had failed and asked the individuals to repeat the process. Investigators suspect that additional SIM cards were activated against the victims’ identities during these repeated attempts, although the individuals concerned received only one connection.

The four suspects were produced before an Islamabad court, which granted the NCCIA two days’ physical remand of each accused for further interrogation.

Officials familiar with the investigation told The Nation that the suspects operated at different locations, including villages and bus stations, where they offered free SIM cards to members of the public. The additional connections allegedly activated against the victims’ identities were subsequently sold to other individuals and used for financial fraud, online scams and other unlawful activities.

At least 70 SIM cards have been recovered so far, the officials said, adding that investigators were also examining the possible involvement of individuals associated with telecommunications franchises in facilitating the alleged illegal activation of the connections.

The first information report (FIR), registered on November 1 at the NCCIA’s Cyber Crime Reporting Centre in Islamabad, names 11 individuals, including suspects whose identities are yet to be established and who are being traced through their WhatsApp accounts, according to the investigation record.

The FIR alleges that the gang activated mobile phone connections against people’s identities without their consent and subsequently used the SIM cards to register fraudulent social media accounts, impersonate individuals and carry out financial scams.

Senior Civil Judge/Judicial Magistrate (West) Malak Aman granted the physical remand to Investigating Officer Babar Ali, a sub-inspector posted at the NCCIA’s Cyber Crime Reporting Centre. The suspects have been directed to be produced before the court again on November 4.

Officials advised members of the public to remain vigilant against unsolicited offers of free SIM cards and obtain mobile connections only through authorised telecommunications franchises. They also urged citizens to ensure that biometric verification is carried out transparently and to avoid allowing repeated scans without a clear explanation of their purpose.

headline: ECP steps up preparations for Islamabad local polls
description: ISLAMABAD - The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has reviewed preparations for the Islamabad local government elections, with the procurement
author: OUR STAFF REPORT
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) has reviewed preparations for the Islamabad local government elections, with the procurement of election materials completed and arrangements for ballot-paper printing put in place.

Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Sikandar Sultan Raja was briefed on Monday by the ECP Secretary and senior officials on the local government system in the federal capital, election procedures for various seats, the measures taken so far and the proposed course of action.

The briefing covered the progress of logistical preparations, with the CEC informed that the procurement of all election materials had been completed and the necessary arrangements for printing ballot papers were in place.

The ECP has also written to the Secretary of the Interior, the Inspector General of Police (IGP) Islamabad and the Deputy Commissioner (DC) Islamabad, seeking the necessary administrative and security arrangements for the polls.

The CEC was informed that the Commission was fully prepared to conduct peaceful local government elections in the federal capital.

Expressing satisfaction with the progress made so far, Sikandar Sultan Raja directed the ECP Secretariat to convene a meeting on November 10 to review the remaining preparations.

The Secretary of the Interior, Chief Commissioner Islamabad and IGP Islamabad have been invited to attend the meeting and brief the Commission on the proposed security plan and other administrative arrangements for the elections.

headline: Sit-in held in Bara to protest killing of two youths in police firing
description: khyber - A sit-in protest was staged by the Political Alliance Bara outside the Bara Press Club at the Tirah IDPs Camp against the alleged killing of two
author: Ahmad Nabi
article_text:
khyber - A sit-in protest was staged by the Political Alliance Bara outside the Bara Press Club at the Tirah IDPs Camp against the alleged killing of two young men belonging to the Shalobar clan of the Afridi tribe in firing by Orakzai district police.

According to a police report, Orakzai police allegedly shot and killed two young men from Bara tehsil, identified as Inayatullah and Muhammad Hussain, a day earlier. The police reportedly alleged that the deceased were involved in smuggling.

Besides residents displaced from Tirah, the protest sit-in was attended by a large number of youths, local tribal elders and political activists. Among those present were Bara Political Alliance (BPA) President Hashim Khan, Shalobar Qaumi Council (SQC) Chairman Lal Nabi Afridi, Bara Traders’ Association President Syed Ayaz Wazir, the alliance’s General Secretary Malik Attaullah and Tirah IDPs Movement Chairman Rahmat Shah.

The protesters expressed deep concern over the killing of the two young men, whom they described as innocent residents of Bara, and demanded a fair, transparent and impartial investigation into the incident.

They also urged the authorities to ensure justice for the bereaved families and take appropriate legal action against those found responsible for the killing.

headline: Hundreds of Shangla youth await KP police appointment orders
description: shangla - Hundreds of unemployed youth from Shangla district, whose names are included in the waiting list for recruitment to the Khyber
author: Aftab Hussain
article_text:
shangla - Hundreds of unemployed youth from Shangla district, whose names are included in the waiting list for recruitment to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Police, have appealed to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Inspector General of Police (IGP) and senior officials of the Home Department to ensure their appointment against vacant posts in accordance with merit and the prescribed rules and regulations.

According to details, these young candidates from the remote and underdeveloped district of Shangla have successfully completed all mandatory stages of the recruitment process for the post of police constable. They have passed the written examination, interview, physical test, running test and medical examination, obtained clearance from the Special Branch and fulfilled all other required formalities. Despite meeting all the eligibility criteria, they have remained on the waiting list for a prolonged period and are still awaiting their appointment orders.

The candidates said that following the recent emergency situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a considerable number of vacancies had been identified in the police force across various districts of the province. In these circumstances, they argued, it was the responsibility of the provincial government and police department to give due consideration to eligible candidates who had already completed all stages of the recruitment process and were placed on the waiting list. They urged the government to review its recruitment policy and consider adjusting waiting-list candidates against available vacant posts instead of initiating a fresh recruitment process.

Talking to The Nation, the waiting-list candidates said they had applied for police constable positions with high hopes, appeared in all the tests after thorough preparation and qualified on merit. They said they had been declared eligible and placed on the waiting list, but no progress had subsequently been made regarding their appointments. The prolonged uncertainty had created frustration and disappointment among hundreds of families in Shangla.

The candidates pointed out that due to the lack of employment opportunities, a large number of young people from Shangla are forced to seek work in coal mines and other mining sectors in different parts of the country, including Balochistan, Sindh and other areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

They said coal mining is among the world’s most dangerous occupations, with precious human lives frequently lost in mine collapses, gas explosions and other accidents. Several young men from Shangla have also lost their lives in mining accidents in recent years, leaving their families in extreme financial hardship.

The waiting-list candidates appealed to Governor Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Faisal Karim Kundi, the IGP, the Secretary of the Home and Tribal Affairs Department and other relevant authorities to take notice of their plight and issue necessary directives for their appointment against vacant posts in accordance with merit and the applicable rules.

They said the Governor, as the constitutional head of the province, should play his role in highlighting the issue of unemployment in underdeveloped districts such as Shangla and urge the relevant departments to review the cases of waiting-list candidates on humanitarian and merit-based grounds.

They further urged the IGP to examine the record of vacant positions in the police department following the recent emergency situation and, if vacancies were available, consider the waiting-list candidates from Shangla who had already qualified the written, physical and running tests, interviews, security clearance and other recruitment formalities, in accordance with the prescribed rules.

They maintained that their appointment would bring dual benefits. On the one hand, it would provide employment to hundreds of jobless young people and help reduce unemployment in the district; on the other, it would strengthen the police force, which they said was facing a shortage of personnel, particularly following the recent emergency situation in the province.

The waiting-list candidates also urged the provincial government to end the uncertainty surrounding their future and announce a clear policy regarding their appointments.

They warned that if their legitimate demand remained unaddressed, they would be compelled to launch peaceful protests and approach higher forums to seek justice.

headline: Women face difficulties as 23 TMA handicraft centres closed in Mardan
description: MARDAN - Women in Mardan are facing immense difficulties following the closure of approximately 23 handicraft centres managed by the Tehsil Municipal
author: Riaz Khan
article_text:
MARDAN - Women in Mardan are facing immense difficulties following the closure of approximately 23 handicraft centres managed by the Tehsil Municipal Administration (TMA) across the district. The closure has deprived women who relied on these centres for self-employment of their primary sources of livelihood.

Expressing concern over the situation, representatives of social and business circles have urged the district administration and municipal authorities to take immediate notice and facilitate the reopening of these centres.

According to sources, the handicraft centres were established in various parts of Mardan to equip women with vocational skills and provide them with dignified employment opportunities.

Women working at these centres were engaged in sewing, embroidery and other handicrafts. However, for various reasons, around 23 centres have been shut down, adversely affecting the economic activities and livelihoods of the women associated with them.

Ayesha Durrani, newly elected President of the Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (WCCI) Mardan, raised the issue during a meeting with officials of the Mardan Municipal Committee and called for the revival of the closed centres. She noted that reopening these facilities would provide women, including those who observe purdah, with opportunities to earn a respectable livelihood within their own localities.

Ayesha Durrani said that women could become economically self-reliant by promoting and marketing the handicraft products they create. She added that the relevant TMA authorities had assured her that prompt measures would be taken to revive the centres, enabling women to resume their work.

Meanwhile, civic and social representatives have urged the Commissioner Mardan, Deputy Commissioner and municipal authorities to investigate the reasons behind the closure of the 23 handicraft centres and take immediate steps to make them operational again.

They said reopening these centres would not only restore employment opportunities for women but also help promote and strengthen the local handicraft industry.

headline: Junaid Anwar calls for aligning education policies with blue economy needs
description: ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Junaid Anwar Chaudhry has called for aligning educational policies with the needs of the blue
author: PR
article_text:
ISLAMABAD - Federal Minister for Maritime Affairs Junaid Anwar Chaudhry has called for aligning educational policies with the needs of the blue economy to develop a skilled workforce and promote sustainable economic growth.

He expressed these views during a meeting with Bahria University Rector Vice Admiral (Retd) Engr Abid Hameed, where they discussed academic cooperation to expand maritime education, strengthen professional skills and improve access to higher education.

The minister said collaboration between the Pakistan Marine Academy (PMA) and Bahria University could help address the shortage of skilled human resources through specialised academic programmes, professional training, research and capacity-building initiatives.

He informed the rector that the process of granting degree-awarding status to PMA had reached its final stage. The proposed upgrade aims to strengthen professional maritime education and bring academic qualifications in the sector closer to international standards.

Identifying key challenges to the development of Pakistan’s blue economy, the minister cited a shortage of skilled workers, weak institutional coordination and a lack of specialised educational programmes.

The meeting also discussed facilitating higher education for deserving students from coastal areas through the proposed Maritime Educational Endowment Fund (MEEF), particularly in maritime-related disciplines.

The fund is envisaged as a long-term financing mechanism for the maritime sector, with projections of building a scholarship corpus of Rs25 billion over 10 years and cumulative disbursements of around Rs12 billion to benefit approximately 65,000 students from all over the country.

Junaid Chaudhry said the initiative could help students from financially disadvantaged coastal and fishing communities access quality education and benefit from emerging employment opportunities in the maritime sector.

He said maritime education was increasingly important given Pakistan’s potential in shipping, port operations, fisheries, marine tourism, offshore energy and other ocean-based industries.

Referring to a 2024 study on the ocean economy, the minister said the sector contributed an estimated 0.4 per cent to Pakistan’s gross domestic product (GDP). He identified inadequate infrastructure, outdated regulations, unsustainable fishing practices and marine pollution as major constraints on its growth.

The minister said the proposed academic partnership also supported the objectives of the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development (2021–2030), which promotes ocean research, scientific cooperation and knowledge-sharing for the sustainable management of marine resources.

Bahria University Rector Vice Admiral (retd) Engr Abid Hameed expressed the university’s readiness to collaborate with PMA in promoting maritime education, research and knowledge-sharing.

The minister said the partnership was also aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 4 (quality education), SDG 8 (decent work and economic growth) and SDG 14 (life below water), which promotes the sustainable use of marine resources and protection of coastal ecosystems.

headline: KP adviser directs to strengthen curriculum review, students’ assessment
description: Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Education, Dr Aamer Abdullah, has directed the Directorate of Curriculum and Teacher
author: Our Staff Reporter
article_text:
Peshawar - Adviser to the Governor of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Education, Dr Aamer Abdullah, has directed the Directorate of Curriculum and Teacher Education (DCTE), Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, to further strengthen its efforts to review the curriculum, effectively assess students’ learning abilities and improve the overall standard of education.

Dr Aamer Abdullah was given a detailed briefing on Monday about the affairs, ongoing activities and performance of the Directorate of Curriculum and Teacher Education, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

During the meeting, DCTE Director Gohar Ali Khan briefed the Education Adviser on the directorate’s mandate, curriculum review process, educational standards and ongoing initiatives. Additional Secretary Elementary and Secondary Education Pir Muhammad, Additional Director Ashfaq Jadoon, Subject Specialist Dr Sahibzada Waqar and Deputy Secretary Hafeezullah also attended the meeting.

During the briefing, Dr Aamer directed the concerned officials to ascertain the reasons behind the Textbook Board’s delay in providing curriculum materials to the directorate for review within the prescribed timeframe. He also directed that a copy of the training module manual developed for the directorate by a private organisation be provided to him.

The Education Adviser stressed the need to explore possible measures to ensure the provision of funds required by the directorate. He said the issue of developing item banks to assess students’ learning abilities at both elementary and secondary levels would also be taken up with the Secretary Elementary and Secondary Education.

Dr Aamer directed the preparation of a practical concept paper within one week to institutionalise the assessment of students’ learning abilities through item banks and make the process simpler, more effective and cost-efficient.

He also sought a detailed report on the meetings of the Joint Academic Council constituted under the Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education.

He directed the concerned officials to provide details of the number of meetings held during the previous year, the decisions taken at those meetings and the proposed schedule of meetings for the current calendar year.

Taking note of the low student participation in assessment tests conducted by the directorate in schools located in the winter zone, the Education Adviser directed officials to identify a sample of schools where student participation in the tests had remained below 50 per cent.

He ordered an inquiry into the reasons for students’ non-participation and directed that a report be submitted within three weeks.

Dr Aamer further directed that proposals addressing the operational requirements of the Directorate of Curriculum and Teacher Education be submitted to the department for further consideration and necessary action.

headline: US, Iran have made progress toward negotiated settlement: Vance
description: US Vice President JD Vance said Monday that Washington has made “progress” in talks with Iran, saying he and President Donald Trump feel
author: Anadolu
article_text:
US Vice President JD Vance said Monday that Washington has made “progress” in talks with Iran, saying he and President Donald Trump feel “pretty good” about reaching a negotiated settlement.

“I actually just spoke with the president of the United States about an hour ago about this,” Vance told reporters. “Look, the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement. We’re going to keep on working at it.”

“The Iranians are always a little unpredictable, and as the president always says, he retains kinetic options. He retains non-kinetic options, but we’ve certainly made some progress. We’ll see if we can make some more,” he said.

Asked whether Iran had been given a deadline before strikes resume, Vance said: “No, we haven’t set deadlines.”

“Having destroyed their nuclear program, we want to make sure they don’t rebuild it or try to rebuild it. That’s what matters most to the United States,” he said.

“We do think that there is a pathway there, but it really does require a firm commitment and a verifiable commitment that they don’t rebuild that nuclear program,” he added.

Vance's remarks came hours after Trump said at the reopening of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington that Iran wants to make a deal to end the conflict, now in its ninth month.

“They want to make a deal, and that could happen,” Trump said, adding that Iran had asked Washington to stop targeting its leaders, “and we will.”

Tensions in the Middle East have remained high since the US and Israel launched attacks against Iran on Feb. 28, triggering Iranian retaliation across the region.

Despite subsequent diplomatic efforts and a memorandum signed by Washington and Tehran in June, tensions have persisted over security arrangements and navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: US to mediate Ukraine-Russia working-level peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10-11
description: The US will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11 as the Trump administration intensifies diplomatic
author: Anadolu
article_text:
The US will mediate working-level negotiations between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Nov. 10–11 as the Trump administration intensifies diplomatic efforts to end the war, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff said Monday

"Discussions will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian efforts and next steps toward peace," Witkoff said on the US social media platform X.

Additionally, Witkoff said American negotiators will meet this week in Brussels with representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the European Union and NATO to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, Europe’s post-war security architecture, and economic opportunities to support Ukraine’s reconstruction.

"We look forward to building on the progress made in Kyiv, Oslo and St. Petersburg toward a comprehensive, durable peace agreement that delivers lasting security for generations to come," he added.

headline: OpenAI names former US army secretary for national security role
description: OpenAI appointed former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as its senior counselor for national security modernization, creating a new position focused on
author: Anadolu
article_text:
OpenAI appointed former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll as its senior counselor for national security modernization, creating a new position focused on advancing the responsible use of artificial intelligence in national security, cybersecurity and defense.

The appointment, announced Monday, will see Driscoll work with OpenAI's senior leadership, government officials, industry executives, academic institutions and international partners to identify opportunities for advanced AI to strengthen national security capabilities, particularly among the US and its allies.

In his newly created role, Driscoll will advise public- and private-sector partners on modernizing policies and strategies to incorporate AI into national security operations. He will also help OpenAI's internal teams better understand the operational requirements and challenges facing national security institutions around the world.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman welcomed the appointment, highlighting the importance of international cooperation in shaping the future of artificial intelligence.

"AI should give people more power over their lives and people should have a say in how it's developed," Altman said.

Driscoll previously served as the 26th Secretary of the United States Army, overseeing the service's operations, modernization programs and resource allocation.

His resignation from the post followed reported disagreements with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth over Army leadership and modernization priorities.

Driscoll described his move to OpenAI as an opportunity to help military personnel and national security institutions benefit from rapidly advancing technology.

"I’m joining OpenAI to help the United States and our allies put this technology to work responsibly, for the people who keep us safe," he said.

headline: Rawalpindi reports 86 confirmed dengue cases, 11 patients hospitalised
description: The District Health Authority Rawalpindi has reported 86 confirmed dengue cases this year, with 11 patients currently hospitalised, including four confirmed
author: NNI
article_text:
The District Health Authority Rawalpindi has reported 86 confirmed dengue cases this year, with 11 patients currently hospitalised, including four confirmed cases.

According to the authority's dengue prevention and control report issued on Monday, November 2, a total of 6,433 patients have been screened at hospitals so far, of whom 5,905 were classified as suspected cases. Two new cases were reported during the last 24 hours.

No dengue-related deaths have been reported so far.

The authority has deployed 415 outdoor and 985 indoor surveillance teams to monitor 17,859 hotspots registered with the Punjab Information Technology Board (PITB). The teams achieved 99 per cent coverage during the previous week.

Meanwhile, enforcement measures against violations of standard operating procedures (SOPs) have resulted in the registration of 2,798 FIRs, sealing of 686 premises and issuance of 2,331 challans. Authorities have also imposed fines amounting to Rs3.156 million.

The highest larva detection was reported in Dhoke Mangtal, Municipal Corporation Rawalpindi, Narar Kahuta, Rawalpindi Cantonment and Dakhali Kahuta.
